summary: Observation of a fixed orange light above the horizon: lack of information.
description: The witness, looking north-northeast at 5:30 PM, "observed an orange light above the horizon from a moving vehicle. The light appeared stationary; it was neither a star, nor the moon, nor a streetlamp." Indeed, there are no very bright stars in that direction, nor is the moon visible, and it is too high in the sky for a streetlamp. Given that the observation occurred shortly after sunset, a temporary reflection of the sun on an aircraft or satellite is possible. The witness stated that the light appeared stationary, but since he was moving, this statement cannot be considered definitive. GEIPAN did not find any commercial airliners on Flightradar24 that could have caused this reflection, but a military aircraft cannot be ruled out. The Calsky sky survey identified several satellite candidates: NOSS satellites that were passing in the witness's direction of observation at that time, and in particular, rocket debris: 3-4 Rocket. These objects, generally faint (magnitude 4 to 6), are known to sometimes "flash." These hypotheses, while plausible, could not be sufficiently substantiated for GEIPAN to adopt them. GEIPAN classifies this somewhat unusual case as category "C": lack of information.

summary: Observation of the appearance of a glow and then a disc-shaped object in the sky: probable observation of the Moon.
description: On December 29, 2013, at approximately 5:45 a.m., a witness on his terrace was intrigued by the presence in the sky of a glow that appeared between clouds, followed by a shimmering disc. The stationary object quickly disappeared behind the clouds. No other reports have been received. The witness described a "slightly tilted, shimmering, light yellow disc" observed for two seconds through a break in the clouds; he indicated a direction of observation "above Cernay, seen from Steinbach towards Mulhouse, therefore south": the star chart shows that the direction of Cernay and Mulhouse is southeast (approximate azimuth: 125°). The star chart indicates the presence of the Moon at its last quarter (a very inclined, thin crescent) at an azimuth of 129° and an elevation of 9°. It is highly probable that the witness did not recognize the Moon due to the clouds and the brevity of the observation. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," a probable lunar observation. Due to the difference in elevation estimates between the witness's report (20th) and that of the Moon (9th), slight doubt remains regarding the presented hypothesis.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of three luminous yellow balls: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On December 27, 2012, around 11:00-11:30 PM, a witness observed three bright yellow orbs moving rapidly west-northeast in the sky. The objects quickly disappeared over the horizon. The observation of three yellow orbs flying for a minute in formation with the wind (a south wind of 20 km/h: weather) on a weekend evening suggests the possibility of Thai lanterns. The witness described "a triangular halo," seemingly inconsistent with typical Thai lanterns; however, the drawing made by the witness (ovni5) closely resembles a photograph of a lantern (see GEIPAN photo). The witness reported a change in trajectory, inconsistent with movement following the wind (a seemingly linear motion): it could be a local gust, or even an illusion in the distance estimation. The apparent speed observed by the witness is consistent with objects flying at 20 km/h at an altitude of approximately 100 meters. Although the witness refutes this hypothesis, GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," a probable observation of Thai lanterns, due to the strong similarity to these objects and the date and time of observation being consistent with the end of a private party.

summary: Observation of the movement of 5 orange balls in the sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: Recent report (February 8, 2015) of a previous observation. On December 24, 2014, at 8:30 PM, a witness observed the slow and silent passage of at least five luminous orange orbs. The observation of orange orbs crossing the sky in a few minutes, on a festive night, strongly suggests the presence of Thai lanterns, probably licked nearby for Christmas. The movement was observed towards the Southeast, while a sustained southwest wind was recorded in Geneva (see weather). In mountainous areas, it is very difficult to model wind at low altitudes. The observed southeastward movement of wind-borne objects is not inconsistent with a southwesterly wind at ground level in Geneva. Furthermore, the witness states that they are observing due south, facing Mont Blanc, while Mont Blanc is actually to the southeast (azure 126°). An uncertainty of approximately 45° is probable. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," indicating a probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the movement of three bright orange luminous balls in the sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On December 22, 2013, at 1:30 a.m., a witness observed from his doorstep the silent passage of two very bright orange orbs moving in a straight line. A third, identical orb then passed over his house and quickly rose into the distance. The witness went to the higher ground above his village to observe the phenomenon, which he would not see again. The observation of luminous orange orbs crossing the sky in the direction of the wind (from the south: see report: weather) on a Saturday night/Sunday morning strongly suggests Thai lanterns, probably released after a festival in the southern part of Esperaza. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of a luminous phenomenon in the clear sky: observation of a parhelion (part of a solar halo).
description: Recent testimony (February 2016) of an earlier observation. On December 21, 2013, between 4:29 PM and 4:33 PM, a witness photographed a luminous phenomenon in the sky that he could not explain. No other testimonies were collected. The observed phenomenon had all the characteristics of a parhelion, part of a solar halo: Parhelion. Parhelion. Météfrance (See photo 6). Because the photos provided are not the original files, GEIPAN could not verify that the angle between the sun and the phenomenon is exactly 22°, but the appearance of the phenomenon, compared to the images on the websites above, leaves no doubt as to its origin. At the time of observation, the sun was at an elevation of 6.30°, which is consistent with this 22° distance between the sun and the phenomenon (see photos). The weather report for Toulouse Blagnac Météociel indicates a southerly wind accompanied by a sharp drop in pressure, thus heralding the arrival of a weather system. This system will bring high-altitude cirrus or cirrostratus clouds, resulting in very cold temperatures, which are conducive to the phenomenon of parhelions (sun dogs) that occur due to the ice crystals in this type of cloud. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A" as an observation of a characteristic parhelion.

summary: Long observation of a bright white point in the night sky; no noise; photographs: lack of information and cross-checking.
description: On December 17, 2013, at approximately 7:15 PM, a witness, from a balcony, was looking at the sky to show his parents the position of the stars using a new astronomy app for smartphones. Intrigued by a bright point of light not listed on the app, the witness, using binoculars, observed a bright, round white dot that remained stationary for about 15 minutes. The witness took photographs of the UFO (images 2 and 3 in the photo folder) and then went inside to warm up. Upon returning to the balcony 5 minutes later, the object had disappeared. No unusual noises were heard. No other witness accounts were collected. This case of observing a stationary white point of light has all the characteristics of a celestial object sighting, but verifications proved negative: firstly, the witness himself, who was using astronomy software, could not identify this point of light among the celestial objects. A check using another software program (Stellarium, see attached document) shows only the star Fomalhaut in the field of view, not very bright (magnitude 1) and, more importantly, too low and too far south relative to the indicated direction. The planet Venus has just set, and Jupiter (magnitude -2.7) is in the northeast. GEIPAN analyzed other hypotheses: - Airplane: the observed object is stationary for too long to be an airplane. - Balloon: the sun sets at 4:44 PM; at this time, only satellites are visible in the sun. - A temporary spotlight on the top of the neighboring hill (motorcycle, car, emergency response): it was noted that there are paths at the top of the hill (see map) where a vehicle could have parked. But the witness mentions an elevation of 45°, significantly higher than the 5° angle at which the hill appears from Baume-les-Dames. -Thai lantern: The color shown in the photo corresponds well to that of a Thai lantern (see illustration "lantern color space"); several possible lantern-letting sites are visible along the observation line: leisure center, hostel, retirement home; lantern-letting usually takes place on weekends and holidays, but the observation occurred on a Tuesday, admittedly close to Christmas. However, this hypothesis is not entirely convincing: Thai lanterns last between 5 and 10 minutes, and this one would be at the limit of that duration. The point-like appearance seen through binoculars is also rather unsuitable: the witness should have been able to distinguish a sphere or an ellipse; the lanterns move with the wind; while it is true that the Besançon weather forecast (see attached document) indicates no wind, it is still surprising to observe a Thai lantern completely motionless. The most plausible hypothesis, strictly speaking, remains that of a Thaean lantern, but with borderline characteristics for this type of phenomenon. GEIPAN cannot definitively confirm this hypothesis. This case remains in category "C" due to a lack of precise data on its position in the sky and a lack of corroborating evidence.

summary: Observation of a bright orange point in the sky and rapid disappearance: lack of information.
description: On Sunday, December 15, 2013, at 6:30 PM, a witness was intrigued by a bright orange object, larger than an airplane, silent, and motionless in the clear sky. After a few minutes, the object moved away and quickly disappeared on an upward trajectory. GEIPAN analyzed two hypotheses for this slowly moving orange object close to the horizon: - An airplane seen head-on, at low altitude, or approaching an airport (Bordeaux-Mérignac, in this case). The witness reportedly saw the airplane approaching and noticed its flashing lights. Radar data from military air traffic control shows significant air activity in the area at that time (see report, unfortunately very illegible, which does not allow for a clear correlation with the observation). In the area bounded northwest of Le Taillan by Sainte-Hélène and northeast by Cubzac, the following flight paths corresponding to civilian aircraft can be observed: - GE 751 heading 200 FL 380 (altitude 12,000m) - GE 962 climbing, passing FL110 (altitude 3,300m) on a heading 020 after a turn south of Saint-Jean-d'Illac and an initial track of 220. - GA474 on a heading 020 FL380 (altitude 12,000m). - Two superimposed flight paths corresponding to an aircraft on a heading 220 descending, passing 3,500' (altitude 1,200m) at 5:13 PM and an aircraft on a heading 040 at 5:46 PM climbing, passing 2,000'. - GE 743 on a heading 160 at 3,800' (altitude 1,300m). -A Thai lantern: the color and appearance match well, as do the duration and elevation; but the light easterly wind should have pushed the lantern to the observer's left, which the witness does not mention. A local wind, slightly different from the one recorded in Mérignac, is also possible. Given the time of observation, at dusk, it could also be a reflection of the sun on a weather balloon launched from Mérignac. Also noted this evening, at very close intervals, are two phenomena of powerful points of light in the sky: - the passage of the International Space Station (ISS) from 6:07 PM to 6:16 PM, from SW to NE (the direction of observation does not correspond well with that indicated by the witness). - and a flash of a few seconds from an Iridium satellite at 6:25 PM due south, just above the horizon. Multiple hypotheses can explain this rather unusual observation, but none perfectly fits the witness's account. GEIPAN classifies this case as C due to a lack of information and cross-checking.

summary: Very long observation of a luminous phenomenon of colour and stationary in the sky: observation of Jupiter.
description: On December 15, 2013, at 11:00 PM, a witness observed the clear sky from their terrace. They saw a stationary, colored luminous phenomenon. The observation lasted several hours, visible to the naked eye and with binoculars. No unusual noises were heard. Only one witness statement was recorded. This observation of a fixed point of light in the sky corresponds to the planet Jupiter, bright in the eastern evening sky. The color changes observed by the witness through binoculars were partly due to atmospheric turbulence (flickering) and partly to the binoculars' optics (a white point of light generally appears iridescent). GEIPAN classifies this case as "A" for the observation of the planet Jupiter.

summary: Observation of the movement of a black dot with two orange trails in the sky: definite observation of airplane condensation trails.
description: The witness went outside his window at 6:30 PM when he saw and filmed a black dot with two orange trails moving across the sky. The phenomenon disappeared over the horizon. The witness posted his video online. The observation of orange trails at dusk in very clear weather suggests contrails from high-altitude aircraft, at a distance of 20 to 100 km. The video leaves no doubt about this phenomenon, which is easily observed in good weather in the West. See also: strange aircraft contrails. GEIPAN classifies this case as A: confirmed observation of contrails.

summary: Observation of the rapid passage of a silver fireball in the sky: probable observation of a bolide (large shooting star).
description: On December 14, 2013, at 3:00 AM, a motorist observed a very rapid passage across the sky of a silver fireball that disappeared to the northeast. No other sightings were reported. The observation of a very bright fireball crossing the sky in less than a second suggests a bolide (a large shooting star), a phenomenon caused by the re-entry into the atmosphere of a fragment of a comet or asteroid. December 14 is a peak date for the Geminid meteor shower: the BOAM network of observers recorded dozens of sightings that night. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of a bolide from the Geminid meteor shower.

summary: Observation, from inside a moving bus, of two small balls connected by a bar in the sky: lack of information.
description: This testimony from a middle school student is rather flimsy: the teenager observed, through the windows of a moving bus, a phenomenon of very small apparent size ("two black balls connected by a black bar," the apparent size of "a bird at 1 km"). Further investigation would yield very little additional information. GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" due to a lack of detailed information and corroboration.

summary: Prolonged observation of a fixed, colored point of light in the sky: probable observation of the star Sirius.
description: witness reports a 30-minute observation made on December 10, 2013, around 1:00 AM. This extended observation of a fixed point of light corresponds to a probable case of mistaken identity with Sirius in the south-southeast: magnitude -1.44, with twinkling. The day's weather forecast weather indicates a strong mistral wind with a very clear and turbulent atmosphere, highly conducive to strong star twinkling. The witness also noticed a point of light in the direction of Orange (southwest) in mid-December between 6:00 PM and 7:00 PM, which is the planet Venus. The photos, taken with a 4-second exposure, show luminous zigzags produced by the operator's movements. In email exchanges with GEIPAN, the witness also reported seeing bright spots near the ground, aligned with Air Base 115 (Orange Caritat Aerodrome), which could be the result of activities on the base. GEIPAN had difficulty obtaining precise directions from the witness regarding the observed bright spots, and therefore was unable to definitively confirm the hypothesis. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of the star Sirius.

summary: Observation during the night of three orange lights in the sky outlining a dark triangular mass: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On December 10, 2013, between 10:06 PM and 10:13 PM, a motorist observed "three large orange lights forming a triangle above a small forest." He observed "a dark mass between these three lights." The lights went out one after the other, and the witness described how "the UFO was also diminishing." Another motorist was interviewed, but only one testimony was recorded. The observation of orange lights for a few minutes strongly evokes Thai lanterns. The fact that the witness saw a dark object between the lights is a common visual illusion (Gestalt theory). It is worth noting that the witness saw this dark shape disappear as the lights went out: this confirms this visual illusion. GEIPAN contacted the gendarmerie, the town hall, and the Château de Vaux-le-Vicomte to try and identify the perpetrators of this lantern release; however, no celebrations were scheduled in the area that evening. It should be noted that the lights were located above a large private park; GEIPAN did not attempt to contact the park's owners, but the release appeared to have taken place further east. The wind was blowing very lightly from the east (see Meteociel report), meaning the witness had the wind at their back and saw the almost stationary objects drifting slightly away. Although lantern releases are quite rare on weekdays, and GEIPAN was unable to identify the perpetrator of this particular release, the witnesses' account remains consistent with this hypothesis. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable sighting of Thai lanterns. The witness did not agree with this hypothesis.

summary: Observation of four bright red luminous balls passing across the sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On December 9, 2013, at 5:15 PM, a witness observed two bright, bright, compact orbs in the clear sky, followed by two others. He took several photos. The orbs behaved like a squadron. They disappeared as they gained altitude. Analysis of the successive images shows luminous orbs arriving from the left of the witness's field of view and moving away in front of him. As the witness was looking southwest and the wind was blowing from the southwest (see report), the hypothesis of wind-borne objects is plausible: it is normal for all objects to follow the same trajectory. These luminous orbs carried by the wind are reminiscent of Thai lanterns. However, it is surprising to see this type of phenomenon on a weekday in the late afternoon: one might think of an early Christmas or Saint Nicholas celebration with children. GEIPAN did not investigate the potential perpetrators of this phenomenon. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B" probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Long observation of a luminous and stationary phenomenon in the sky: observation of Venus.
description: On December 8, 2013, starting at 5:15 PM, several people observed a unique, spherical phenomenon in the south-southwest sky, which intrigued them. Very bright, the phenomenon appeared stationary in the clear sky. It was observed until around 8:00 PM. The very bright point of light that the witness observed for a long time in the southwest in the early evening was undoubtedly the planet Venus, which was particularly bright at that time. Excellent weather conditions made the sight surprising for the witness. The witness classified this case as "A": observation of the planet Venus.

summary: Observations of a bright glow in the sky: observations of an airplane contrail.
description: On December 1, 2013, around 5:00 PM, people walking on the coastal path in Bandol were intrigued by the presence of a bright glow in the sky to the west of the sun. The glow persisted after sunset and revealed two bright, stationary points of light, visible to the naked eye, yellow-orange in color. They faded after 15 minutes. Only one witness account was recorded. Red-orange trails at sunset clearly resembled airplane contrails, made bright by the backlighting. See: Strange airplane contrails. The attached "flightradar24" report indicates the aircraft visible that day. Aircraft contrails are visible up to 120 km in these excellent visibility conditions. Due to the distance and the direction of the departing aircraft, the contrail appears at a very shallow angle, giving a compressed perspective of the phenomenon. For the same reasons, the angular velocity of the contrail appears low. GEIPAN classifies this case as A, meaning it is perfectly identified.

summary: Brief observation of a yellow light and black smoke in the sky preceded by a loud explosion: probable observation of a flare.
description: On November 28, 2013, at 12:10 PM, a motorist heard a bang and immediately observed a large flash of yellow fire in the sky above a field, surrounded by black smoke. The phenomenon quickly disappeared. Another person, on a road adjacent to the one where the witness was located, appears to have looked in the same direction at that moment. No other witness statements were collected. The description of the observation, particularly the sequence (bang followed by a bright, fire-colored flash accompanied by a black cloud), all within a short duration (< 1 minute), is consistent with the launch of a detonating and/or illuminating rocket (see the video of a detonating rocket for a blank-firing pistol). The origin of the launch cannot be determined, but it is possible that it was the motorist who was on the road parallel to the one where the witness was (and who was also looking at the sky). Consequently, GEIPAN classifies this case as B: flare.

summary: Discontinuous observation of a luminous phenomenon in the clear sky: observation of Venus and aircraft.
description: On November 27, 2013, at 6:00 PM, two people intermittently observed a luminous phenomenon in the sky. The observation lasted 1 hour and 30 minutes. This observation unfolded in three phases: - observation of a luminous point in the Northeast (two large yellow lights with a red light in the middle), initially stationary, then disappearing behind a building: this strongly resembled an airplane or helicopter seen from the front, with its searchlights on. - observation by the witness's son, who saw a luminous point pass over the house, which was "swaying". At 6:02 PM and 6:05 PM, two aircraft were observed flying at high altitude over the area (see the Flightradar readings and the military radar track on the Geoportail map, in UTC). Helicopter activity was also noted at this time, between 6:12 PM and 6:30 PM, above the high-voltage power line located between Quinssaines and Nouhant, 7 km southwest of the observation site. The witness's description is not precise enough to determine which aircraft was actually observed. Towards the end of the observation, a very bright point was seen to the southwest, remaining almost stationary for over an hour: this was undoubtedly the planet Venus, which was particularly bright at that time (Magnitude -4.7). The varying appearance of the photos taken by the witness is explained by inconsistent focus settings and camera shake during the shooting process. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": observation of Venus for the end of the observation, and probable observation of planes and/or helicopters for the beginning of the observation.

summary: Observation in the sky of four stationary oblong luminous shapes: observation of airplane contrails at sunset.
description: On Tuesday, November 26, 2013, around 5:30 PM, a witness was intrigued by the presence of lights with a peculiar shape in the sky. The phenomenon of oblong shapes, seemingly stationary in the sunset sky (see witness's photo), clearly resembles contrails illuminated by the setting sun (the sun set at 5:00 PM at an azimuth of 240° SW). See the Flightradar report, which shows an aircraft that could be the source of this contrail. See: Strange contrails These contrails are visible from nearly 80 km away in clear weather: at this distance, the aircraft's angular displacement appears very small, especially if it is moving away from or towards the witness. When the sun is too far below the horizon, the contrails, no longer illuminated, become invisible. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A" – observation of aircraft contrails.

summary: Observation of the silent passage under the clouds of a round, very bright and yellow-orange phenomenon: lack of information.
description: On November 23, 2013, at 6:45 PM, a person observed a very bright, round, orange-yellow object moving silently and straight across the cloudy sky for 15 seconds. Traveling west-southwest, the object was quickly obscured by the corner of the house. The sighting of an orange-yellow sphere moving horizontally on a Saturday evening might suggest a Thai lantern released at the start of a festival. However, the witness observed the object in a sparsely populated area, and there is no visible sign that the lantern, carried by the northwest wind, could have been licked. The weather report for Rodez indicated a strong northwest wind and cloudy skies. (See: weather. Given the brevity of the observation (15 seconds), it is difficult to confirm or refute this hypothesis. No other eyewitness accounts were collected. A ball lightning phenomenon is also possible, but very unlikely at this time of year. However, the weather was very unsettled that day. GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" due to a lack of information.

summary: Observation of a sparkling white light in the sky: probable sighting of Venus.
description: witness reported a prolonged observation of a white light in the clear sky that appeared to twinkle blue at times. No sound was heard. No other reports were collected. This long and repeated observation of a very bright point of light near the southwest in the early evening has all the characteristics of an observation of the planet Venus, which is particularly visible at this time of year (Magnitude -4.6). The variability in brightness is due to atmospheric variability, probably caused by the proximity of the ocean. The indicated observation directions correspond to the planet's position (see witness map and GEIPAN map), however, with some inconsistencies: the witness indicates an elevation of approximately 45° (whereas Venus was around 10°), and observes a noticeable movement of the phenomenon in the sky. These inconsistencies are probably due to a lack of precise reference points during the observation and the multitude of observation locations. (The witness mentions the Moon, which was absent at that time on November 22nd, but specifies in a separate message that it was on Tuesday the 19th that they saw the Moon). GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of the planet Venus.

summary: Observation of a stationary green glow in the cloudy sky: laser animation.
description: On Saturday, November 16, 2013, at 11:35 PM, a witness observed a stationary light in the cloudy sky above a stadium, remaining visible after the stadium lights had been turned off. This resident of Pau, looking towards Juraneon, thought it might be a laser but couldn't identify its source. That evening, there was a "Cultures électronique-Soleils numériques" festival with a green laser installation on the Guindalos hillside in Gelos, south of Pau. The program is available at festival Acces(s). This is a Class A case: observation of a laser animation

summary: Observation of the rectilinear and then curved movement of a multicolored light in the sky: lack of information.
description: On Tuesday, November 12, 2013, from 6:55 a.m. to 7:15 a.m., a witness observed a multicolored light, initially stationary, then moving in a straight line and later in a curve at the speed of a hot air balloon. The luminous phenomenon was seen as a vertical beam. No unusual noise was heard. No other witness statements were collected. Given the information gathered: - Area suitable for flights of small motorized aircraft - Behavior similar to the movement of such aircraft - Night flight regulations respected But also: - No similar lighting signal found - Nature and behavior of part of the UAP unknown - No events related to the use of ultralight aircraft or helicopters reported on the day of the observation This case is classified as C e, due to a lack of information to validate either hypothesis, as confusion with an ultralight aircraft or a helicopter remains possible under certain conditions. It is possible that another cause is involved. This testimony is quite consistent: very precise but without photographs or videos. The observation is strange because it is rather unusual, because although, given its movement and geographical location, the UFO could be considered a motorized craft—helicopter, ultralight aircraft, or drone—the lights observed, as well as some of its physical characteristics described in the testimony, do not correspond to what is known about such craft; these varied colors could possibly be explained by atmospheric glare. Due to the only moderate strangeness of this sighting, GEIPAN did not deem it necessary to conduct a more in-depth investigation. Information subsequently provided by other witnesses could lead to a change in this conclusion.

summary: Observation of an intense light and confirmation of the presence of a luminous intensity on photographs: observation of parhelion.
description: On November 10, 2013, between 4:59 PM and 5:00 PM, a witness observed a luminous intensity for 10 minutes, impossible to see directly. Taking photographs of the Parc de Sceaux, the witness then noticed in the photos a luminous trail, first white, then red, above the horizon, which he could not explain. The observation of luminous phenomena at sunset supports the hypotheses related to this phenomenon. The angle between the sun and the phenomenon was approximately 22°, an angle conducive to the phenomenon of a parhelion (sun dog). This phenomenon occurs in the presence of high-altitude ice clouds, which could be possible given the sky filled with cirrus clouds and a weather report indicating cold and dry conditions. It can also occur on aircraft contrails: the observed shape and the heavy air traffic also make this origin possible. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": observation of a parhelion. Note: the green spots observed in the photos are effects of internal reflections within the camera lens (lens flare).

summary: Observation of the slow movement in the sky of an elongated shape with blinking: lack of information.
description: On November 8, 2013, at 5:40 AM, a witness lying in bed observed through a window the very slow passage of an elongated shape with flashing lights across the sky. The UFO was heading southeast. No noise was heard during the 15-minute observation; the phenomenon gradually disappeared. Only one witness account was collected. This observation report is very brief: the witness describes neither the shape, nor the color, nor the brightness of what they saw. The strangeness of the phenomenon is rather low, since the witness initially thought they saw an airplane; it is only the apparent slowness of the phenomenon that makes it seem strange: a relative angle of movement compared to the witness could possibly explain this surprising effect. This somewhat strange and inconsistent case is classified as "C" due to a lack of information.

summary: Filmed observation of an orange luminous phenomenon and numerous oblique traces also of orange color in the sky: observation of airplane contrails.
description: On Wednesday, November 6, 2013, at 6:00 PM, several people were intrigued by the presence of a fireball in the sky, followed by diagonal trails of the same color (bright orange). The witness filmed the scene. Only one witness account was recorded. The observation of bright orange trails in the sunset sky clearly suggested contrails from distant aircraft illuminated by the sun already below the horizon. The video confirms this hypothesis, as does the "Casperflights" report of airliners, which were very numerous in the area at that time (Northern Europe/Spain-Portugal-Morocco traffic). The first video (a descending vertical trail) corresponds to an aircraft moving away from the witnesses, while the other horizontal trails correspond to aircraft traveling from north to south, about 50 km west of Pau. Exceptional weather conditions made this spectacle particularly remarkable that evening. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": observation of aircraft contrails.

summary: Long observations by several witnesses in different places of lights with twinkling and slow movement in the sky: mistaking them for very bright stars (Jupiter, Sirius, Vega, Rigel).
description: On the night of November 6-7, 2013, a resident (T1) of Tallard (05) observed and filmed several lights in the sky starting at 11:55 PM. He contacted the gendarmerie and civil aviation authorities by telephone to report the events. A patrol was dispatched to the witness's location, and all observers made further observations between 12:30 AM and 12:54 AM from Tallard. At 1:00 AM, a gendarme in Gap (T2) spotted a shimmering, luminous sphere in the southeast direction. At 1:40 AM, T1 and the gendarmerie patrol ceased their observation. Around 2:00 AM, T2 also stopped observing. The video recording made by T1 is of very poor quality: the images are blurry and zoomed in. The observation took place from two different locations (see investigation report) under a relatively clear sky. The observations of the various UAPs (Unidentified Aerial Phenomena) exhibit all the characteristics of astronomical observations, given the description of the UAPs (flickering lights) and the length of the observation periods (more than two hours from Tallard (05), approximately one hour from Gap (05)). The twinkling of the UAPs is perfectly consistent with the twinkling of stars, a natural phenomenon caused by high-altitude winds. The twinkling of stars is all the stronger the lower the celestial bodies are on the horizon, which is indeed the case with the various UAPs observed that night. Moreover, the presence of significant mountain ranges (the Alps) in the immediate vicinity of the observation sites only reinforces the high-altitude winds responsible for this twinkling. The very high degree of consistency between the true positions of the brightest celestial bodies then present in the sky and those of the observed UAPs leaves no doubt that the observation was a mistake. Of low strangeness and high consistency (multiple witnesses, video recording), this case appears to be a very probable case of mistaken identity involving celestial bodies: Rigel, Jupiter, Vega, and Sirius. Furthermore, these celestial bodies were directly visible in the directions indicated by the witnesses, and the sky was clear. The twinkling of the UFOs and the movement of UFO 4 are also perfectly consistent with celestial bodies. This case is Class A, a case of mistaken identity involving very bright celestial bodies (Jupiter, Sirius, Vega, and Rigel).

summary: Prolonged observation of an intense orange light in the sky: probable observation of an airplane contrail.
description: witness observed an intense, elongated light in the sky, a light, slightly orange color, mimicking the reflection of the sunset on an airplane fuselage. The bright point remained visible for a long time. The observation of a luminous orange shape due west shortly after sunset strongly suggests an object at high altitude illuminated by the setting sun. The planet Venus is located further south than the direction indicated by the witness and should appear circular and white, rather than elongated and orange. A distant contrail (between 40 and 80 km) from an airplane flying at 12,000 m, 50 km from Paris, traveling from south to north, could have given this impression. Due to the distance, these contrails appear very small and seem almost motionless. As the sun sinks below the horizon, these contrails become invisible. See also Strange airplane contrails. This case is a "B" class probable airplane contrail observation.

summary: Short observation of the rectilinear and rapid movement of an oval-shaped object with two round wings: probable observation of a child's ball.
description: The witness, who was flying a kite, observed a metallic gray, oval-shaped object with two rounded wings high in the sky. Its trajectory was very straight and its speed particularly rapid. Due to his activity, the witness was more or less facing away from the wind, looking towards the East or Northeast (with a West to Northwest wind). The witness saw the object pass over the kite and disappear to the North (according to the questionnaire) or East (according to the witness's diagram, named stbenoit.jpg). The object behaved like a wind-borne object (with a sustained wind of 26 to 44 km/h), probably flying quite low (100 to 200 m) to appear very fast to the witness. The shape drawn by the witness resembles the silhouette of a Mickey Mouse balloon (see Mickey Mouse balloon). The witness perceived the object's trajectory to be at a 45° angle to the wind direction: this discrepancy can be explained, on the one hand, by the uncertainty of the estimate, and on the other hand, by the variability of the wind depending on the weather (see weather report) and altitude. This observation is not very strange: the object moves in a straight line, and most likely with the wind. This very brief eyewitness account from a single witness is of average reliability (a photograph or a second witness statement would have allowed for confirmation or refutation of the hypothesis). GEIPAN classifies this observation as "B" as a probable observation of a child's balloon.

summary: Observation of the very rapid and silent movement of three luminous objects in the sky: lack of information.
description: On October 30, 2013, at 11:38 PM, a witness observed three luminous objects flying silently at the same altitude and at high speed. The objects disappeared above the rooftops. The observation of points of light moving very quickly in a straight line for a few seconds suggests shooting stars or fireballs. This observation is remarkable because there are three objects moving in parallel. It could be a meteor that broke into three pieces upon reentry. The slight lateral movement of one of them could be a perceptual illusion called autokinesis (see The Perception of the Movement of a Point of Light in the Sky). The BOAM network (see: BOAM) recorded numerous fireballs last night, including one precisely at 22:38 UTC, but they were observed to the east, from eastern France; therefore, it is not the same event. This network does not have a camera near Sablé-sur-Sarthe (72). However, the frequency of events last night only indicates a significant probability of fireball observation. Nevertheless, given the brevity of the observation, the single witness account, and the fact that there were three objects, this fireball observation hypothesis is quite fragile. GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" pending possible corroboration.

summary: Successive observations on the same evening of luminous red-colored phenomena in the sky: probable observations of Thai lanterns.
description: On October 30, 2013, between 6:50 PM and 8:30 PM, three witnesses observed a red luminous phenomenon in the sky, which appeared and then seemed to hover above a nearby forest. The phenomenon disappeared, only to reappear later, still fixed in the sky. It eventually faded away like a halogen lamp. Two people gave witness statements. The observation of orange spheres in the sky for a few minutes is reminiscent of Thai lanterns, but this case is unusual in several respects: - it was not a Saturday night. It was Halloween, which may have been an occasion for a licking. - The objects appear stationary: the witness, interviewed by telephone, was looking towards the Northwest (see map), that is to say, with his back to the light Southeast wind (see the weather report for Île d'Oléron) and saw an object carried by the wind slowly move away from the witness and appear motionless. - A second object appears in the same place 15 minutes later: it is possible, as is often the case, that there were several lantern releases, which would have followed exactly the same trajectory. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of two luminous phenomena in the night sky: lack of information.
description: On October 28, 2013, at 10:50 PM, a witness driving on the D342 in the town of Taluyers observed a red light in the clear sky in their rearview mirror. They made a second observation at 11:03 PM on the D63 near the Rosseon sign (in the town of Mornant): an orange, spherical object with a tail quickly crossed their field of vision through their windshield. Other people were on the road, but no other witness statements were collected. Of moderate strangeness and weak consistency (single witness, poor quality of testimony, uncertainty regarding the date), this case is too imprecise for each observation to be formally identified. It is not the witness's visual perception that is at issue, but rather their interpretation of the observation based on their feelings (surprise, stress, fatigue, night driving). This case is classified as Class C due to a lack of data.

summary: Observation at a fair of the movement of a dark object under the cloud layer: probable observation of the movement of a festive balloon inflated with helium.
description: witness at a fair on October 27, 2013, observed and photographed a black object moving very slowly beneath the clouds. Several people subsequently observed the phenomenon, but only one eyewitness account was recorded. The witness described the object as black to gray, ovoid, changing shape, resembling a complexly shaped balloon rotating in the wind. Because it was observed against a clear sky, it necessarily appeared very dark, regardless of its actual color. The wind recorded at Luc-Cannet des Maures (Source: Meteociel) was variable, light, easterly in the morning, northerly at midday, and westerly in the late afternoon; this does not perfectly match the observed movement, but it is extremely difficult to estimate wind speed in mountainous areas with light winds. Despite this uncertainty, given the similarity of the object to a balloon, probably related to the local festival, GEIPAN classifies this somewhat strange case in category "B": probable observation of a festive balloon inflated with helium.

summary: Observation of a very bright and fixed white point in the sky: observation of Venus.
description: On October 25, 2013, at 8:00 PM, two people observed a bright, stationary white point in the sky. To the southwest at the time of observation, they saw the planet Venus, particularly bright at that time (magnitude -5, its maximum), under a very clear sky (visibility 35 km) despite some clouds (see Meteociel report). This created exceptional conditions that made observing the planet remarkable. A passing cloud cover then obscured the planet from the witnesses. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": observation of Venus. Note: The witness reported an altitude of 45° above the horizon, while the photograph shows a much lower elevation, consistent with the actual elevation of the planet at 8°30'.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of about ten white dots in the morning sky: probable bird sighting.
description: On October 23, 2013, at 7:30 a.m., a witness was surprised to see about ten bright lights moving silently across the sky in three successive waves. He completely ruled out the possibility that they were Thai lanterns, fighter jets, or any kind of light reflection. No other witnesses reported seeing them. The likely explanation is a flock of migratory birds. At this time of year, many birds migrate from north to south along the main migratory flyways. One of these flyways passes east of Callac. Generally, migratory birds fly between 100 and 400 meters in altitude. However, with headwinds, as was the case here, the birds lower their altitude, making them more visible at dusk or dawn. In particular, Brent Geese migrate from the North to the Gulf of Morbihan during this period. Their plumage is primarily brown, black, and white. At night, illuminated by the moon, only the white part remains visible, and the yellowish color mentioned by the witness corresponds to the color of the light reflected by the moon. The wings, being dark, are not visible in the darkness. The observation is therefore not very unusual. The only slight oddity comes from the last light, which was more intense than the others (but it should be noted that this point was not present at the time of the observation and the questionnaire and was mentioned by the witness during the investigation, which could also result from a false memory phenomenon three years later). This observation is of moderate consistency initially (only one witness, no photos or videos) and is reinforced by a cognitive interview. GEIPAN therefore classifies the case as B, probable observation of birds (several groups of Brent Geese or other migrating birds).

summary: Observation of the silent SN movement of a dark object in the shape of a half-dome with hanging protrusions: probable observation of the passage of a festive balloon.
description: On October 22, 2013, at 10:40 PM, a witness observing the clear sky was intrigued by the south-south passage of a dark, dome-shaped object with dangling protrusions. The very brief observation (less than 10 seconds) did not allow the witness to take a photograph. The silent object disappeared into the darkness of the night sky. Based on information gathered through the questionnaire and the interview with the witness, GEIPAN classifies this case as B, suggesting it was likely a helium-filled party balloon, possibly of the ladybug type, that had escaped its owner's control.

summary: Sighting in the sky of colored lights outlining a triangular shape: probable sighting of a passenger plane.
description: On Tuesday, October 22, 2013, at approximately 7:50 p.m., a motorist was intrigued by an object in the sky. The witness described a triangular-shaped object composed of three bright points of light: red, green, and blue. The object was stationary at first, then moved slowly and silently. The lights turned white, and it disappeared. Only one witness account was recorded. Given the objective elements gathered in the attached investigation report—namely, the highly probable presence of a scheduled flight at the time and azimuth in question, the delimitation of the triangular shape by lights identical to the aircraft's navigation lights, the movement of the UAP identical to that of the flight in question, along the witness's line of sight, and the disappearance of the UAP behind clouds, first temporarily, then permanently, in the same way that a high-altitude aircraft is obscured by patchy cloud layers—we can conclude that the case concerns the probable sighting of an airliner observed under specific conditions. This case is classified as category B, as the probable sighting of an airliner operating the scheduled Venice/London route, illuminated by its navigation lights, and temporarily obscured by cloud layers. It is the uncertainty about the precise time of the plane, and the doubt about the colours of the lights reported by the witness that prevent this case from being classified as A.

summary: Observation of a set of equidistant lights forming a triangle: a definite astronomical mistake with the Hyades cluster.
description: On October 20, 2013, between midnight and 1:00 AM, two people walking together were intrigued by the presence in the sky of a group of equidistant lights forming a triangle. Only one witness account was recorded. Of moderate strangeness and consistency, this case appears to be a clear case of mistaken identity with the Hyades star cluster. Moreover, the Hyades were perfectly visible along the axis indicated by the witness, and the position of the lights composing the UFO perfectly matches that of the stars in the cluster. The UFO appears as only a single orange light, much like the star Aldebaran, a neighbor of the Hyades. It is not the witness's visual perception that is at issue, but rather the witness's interpretation of their observation based on their feelings (surprise, fatigue, walking at night, and the presence of clouds that could give the UFO an illusion of movement). This case is class A, definitely a misunderstanding with the Hyades cluster.

summary: Observation of the presence and movement of a silent triangle, dark in color, with a luminous outline: lack of information.
description: The witness, awakened by the rain, went out into his yard and observed a silent, dark-colored triangle with a luminous outline. The object rose and disappeared into the clouds. The described observation did not correspond to any known phenomenon. As this observation did not suggest any of the usual misinterpretations, GEIPAN (the French National Gendarmerie's Office for the Study of Unidentified Aerial Phenomena) commissioned an investigator to interview the witness on site, but the witness did not respond to this offer. Given that the observation was brief and occurred in the middle of the night, upon the witness waking, a possible explanation could be a hypnopompic hallucination (which occurs upon waking); see the end of the article: Hallucination). However, the witness indicated that he was already fully awake before getting up. One could also consider the possibility of retinal persistence if the witness turned on the light (fluorescent tubes?) between their room and the courtyard. The investigation could have confirmed or refuted one or the other of these hypotheses, or opened up new possibilities. Pending further information or corroboration, this case remains classified as "C".

summary: Sighting of a dark oval object above the trees: probable hoax: the sighting may be real, but the photo is certainly not authentic.
description: On October 16, 2013, at 6:00 PM, a witness on a scooter returning to Vienne-en-Arthies (95) stopped and observed an oval-shaped object above the trees. The object was initially stationary and then moved slowly. The witness had time to take photographs before the object suddenly disappeared. Given the certainty that the reference photograph for this testimony is not authentic (see detailed report), the credibility and consistency of this case are very low, despite an apparently sincere observation report. Following this assessment of the photograph, GEIPAN did not deem it necessary to pursue further investigation. GEIPAN classifies this case as B: probable hoax: the observation may be real, but the photograph is certainly not authentic.

summary: Multiple observations by pilots and ground witnesses of the rapid passage of a blue-green luminous phenomenon in eastern France: observation of an atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid.
description: On October 13, 2013, four pilots (see the estimated positions of the four aircraft on the aeronautical questionnaire) observed a powerful luminous phenomenon in eastern France. This phenomenon was also observed on the ground (see press article) and by the Chaligny camera (near Nancy) of the BOAM network. This phenomenon, called a bolide, was characterized as an atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid (meteorite fall). GEIPAN classifies this case as "A".

summary: Observation of a luminous phenomenon in the sky: lack of information.
description: On October 11, 2013, around 10 p.m., several people observed a bright yellow light in the cloudy sky. The light flickered and then disappeared instantly. Only one witness reported this. GEIPAN investigated several hypotheses for this observation of a fixed yellow light for two minutes: - Star or planet: the witness reported a very cloudy sky, as did the weather reports from Nîmes and Avignon. Furthermore, in the direction close to that indicated by the witness (Southeast), there were no very bright celestial objects likely to be visible through a thin layer of cloud. - Reflection of the sun on a geostationary satellite: no such event was recorded for that time (it would have been around 8 p.m.), and the cloud cover must have obscured this phenomenon. - Thales' lantern: the light as described by the witness could correspond to a Thales' lantern. A Friday evening is quite conducive to this type of licking. To be seen as stationary, there would need to be a tailwind (NW) or a headwind (SE) to the observer, which isn't exactly the case as it's a northerly wind. This hypothesis, however, remains to be considered. - Aircraft: the light as described by the witness could correspond to the landing lights of an aircraft approaching or taking off from Avignon. The Flightradar24 website, which lists civilian aircraft equipped with transmitting beacons, doesn't mention any aircraft in this area at this time, but a military aircraft, seen head-on, remains a possible hypothesis. GEIPAN does not have the information to confirm either of the last two hypotheses, which themselves remain tentative. GEIPAN classifies this somewhat unusual case in category "C" due to a lack of information.

summary: Daytime observation of 9 bright points in the sky, of low intensity, forming a sort of checkerboard and gradually disappearing: probable observation of festive balloons.
description: Recent report (January 18, 2015) of a previous observation. On October 11, 2013, at 10:08 AM, a witness observed nine faint points of light forming a sort of checkerboard pattern. The points gradually disappeared. The witness took photos. No other reports were collected. The witness observed the area towards the Northwest (see their photos and the Google map) and saw the points moving slightly from their right to their left. The wind recorded in Nîmes-Garons was from the North and light (see report). Points of light moving in a straight line across the sky suggest balloons reflecting the sun. Their movement is consistent with the North wind; October 10th was a festival day in Aigues-Mortes, so a balloon release would not be surprising. These balloons, carried by the north wind, approach the witness horizontally but move away vertically as they gain altitude, until they burst. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of celebratory balloons. Given the low unusualness of the case, and the delay of more than a year between the observation and its reporting, GEIPAN did not conduct any local investigations into the origin of this lecher.

summary: Observation of the silent passage of a dark object in the sky: probable observation of the passage of a helium-filled balloon.
description: On October 9, 2013, at approximately 5:45 PM, two witnesses observed a dark flying object in the sky. Its upper part was oval-shaped, and its lower part cylindrical. It was about 50 meters high and moving slowly and silently. The observation of a low-altitude object moving regularly and silently with the wind (a west wind that day of approximately 15 km/h according to Meteociel) strongly suggests a helium-filled balloon, perhaps a child's balloon. These objects have very varied shapes and, when observed against the light, generally appear black. GEIPAN classifies this unusual case as category "B": probable observation of a helium-filled balloon.

summary: Observation of the peculiar movement of a white dot in the sky: probable observation of two planes crossing paths, flying at a medium altitude and illuminated by the setting sun.
description: On Monday, October 7, 2013, at approximately 6:30 PM, a motorist on the A63 motorway was intrigued by the movement of a white dot in the sky. The witness saw it move south, disappear, and then appear to move north. No flashing lights indicating an aircraft were visible. At 6:30 PM, the setting sun was at an azimuth of 251° and an altitude of 9° 55'. It illuminated the aircraft laterally; the wings, not lit from above or below, appeared invisible. Not all aircraft produce contrails: those flying below approximately 7,000 meters did not. According to the Flightradar24 website, numerous flights were observed along this route, most above 10,000 meters, but some at lower altitudes (see attached report). At 6:52 PM (civil time), two aircraft crossed paths in the observation area. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of two aircraft, flying at medium altitude and illuminated by the setting sun.

summary: Observation of a bright orange static light at low altitude: observation of a streetlamp.
description: On October 3, 2013, at approximately 10:05 PM, a witness was intrigued by the presence of a bright orange semicircle in the low-altitude sky. The observation lasted five minutes. More than a year after the event, and after investigating various possibilities of misinterpretation, GEIPAN (the French National Group for the Study of Explosive Orbital Problems) offered the witness an on-site investigation. The witness replied that he had discovered the source of the phenomenon himself: a distant streetlamp. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": observation of a streetlamp.

summary: Observation of the movement of two bright points advancing symmetrically at the same speed: probable observation of Yaogan satellites.
description: witness observed two bright, fixed points of light moving silently in a symmetrical fashion and at the same speed on Thursday, October 3, 2013, at 7:40 PM. The observation of two star-like points of light, moving continuously across the sky in a straight line, strongly suggests the passage of two satellites. A check with the Calsky.com website shows that the Chinese Yaogan17 observation satellite trio, launched on September 1, 2013, passed by at the same time on a trajectory corresponding to the observation. These satellites are known to reflect relatively little sunlight (magnitude 5 to 6), but can probably be oriented in such a way that they become brighter. See a video of other satellites in the Yaogan series Yaogan satellites. This could explain why the witness sees 2 and not 3. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B" - very probable observation of Yaogan satellites.

summary: Observations of the fall of a luminous, round object with green trails: atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid.
description: On October 2, 2013, around 10:00 PM, two teenagers observed a round, luminous object with green trails falling towards the town of Rantswiller. This case was handled by the Sierentz (68) gendarmerie, which meticulously gathered essential information and conducted an exemplary investigation with the relevant authorities. In addition to this information, the www.boam.fr database indicates a fireball captured to the southwest by a camera located in Chaligny (54), near Nancy, at 9:57 PM that same day. It is also worth noting (see attached document) that several other large fireballs were observed that night. The event was noted by several observers in the Paris region who reported it on the website "Ciel des hommes" Paris meteorite. There is some variation in the reports regarding the time of the phenomenon, ranging from "around 10:00 PM" to 10:15 PM. The witness from Walbach indicated "around 10:15 PM," but he called his godmother at 10:03 PM, just after the observation: this precise information, accurately recorded by the police, allows for a certain correlation between this observation and the fireball recorded on the Chaligny camera at 9:57 PM. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": confirmed observation of a fireball caused by the re-entry into the atmosphere of a meteoroid (natural meteorite).

summary: Observation of a light on the horizon followed by the passage of flashing lights in the night sky: lack of information.
description: On October 1, 2013, at approximately 9:30 PM, a witness observed a light on the horizon from her home. Accompanied by her partner, she witnessed the disappearance of the UFO (Unidentified Flying Object) followed by the rapid passage of three flashing lights. This passage was accompanied by a resonating noise, resembling that of an aircraft. Of moderate strangeness and weak consistency (single witness, short observation duration), this case could be a case of mistaken identity involving the star Arcturus and then a formation of aircraft. However, the lack of precision in the testimony (difference in direction between the account and the sketches), and the lack of information on air traffic, prevent formal identification of the UFO. It is not the witness's visual perception that is at issue, but rather the witness's interpretation of the observation based on their feelings (surprise, nighttime observation). This case is classified as Class C, due to a lack of information allowing verification of the hypotheses put forward.

summary: Observations of evolutions in a cloudy sky of bluish-white lights: probable observation of a light animation coming from a Skyrose type projector.
description: On October 1, 2013, between 11:15 PM and 11:25 PM, a witness observed two bluish-white lights moving together randomly from their home, passing through the clouds. Ten minutes later, the phenomena disappeared. Two hours later, identical lights appeared and then vanished just as suddenly. The witness took some photos. The witness's description of bluish-white lights moving together randomly, their light passing through the clouds, strongly suggests a light show like those used in nightclubs. The witness's photos clearly show that the luminous patches are only visible on the clouds, evidence of light being projected from the ground. It should be noted, however, that Wednesday evening is an unusual day for this type of display. Due to the relatively minor nature of this phenomenon, GEIPAN did not conduct a thorough investigation to determine its precise origin. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of a luminous animation, skyrose type.

summary: Observation of the silent passage of eight red objects in the sky on the same trajectory: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On September 28, 2013, at approximately 9:00 PM, a witness observed eight bright red objects crossing the sky from east to west along the same trajectory. The observation of several red shapes moving along the same path in the same direction as the wind (from the southeast) on a Saturday evening strongly suggests the release of Thai lanterns (flying lanterns). GEIPAN classifies this unusual case as category "B," indicating a probable sighting of Thai lanterns.

summary: Successive observations of the silent and rectilinear movement of an orange ball: probable observation of the passage of Thai lanterns.
description: On Friday, September 27, 2013, between 10:15 PM and 10:30 PM, a witness at home observed the successive passage of an orange sphere across the cloudy sky. The object moved silently from east to west. The description of the observation has all the characteristics of a Thae lantern: orange spheres following one another along the same horizontal trajectory, depending on the local wind (a steady east wind of approximately 15 km/h according to www.meteociel.fr), on a weekend evening. The photographs, of rather poor quality, provide little information. GEIPAN classifies this somewhat unusual case as category "B": observation of two successive Thae lanterns.

summary: Observation of the straight and rapid passage of a luminous ball then with a change of trajectory: lack of information and cross-checks.
description: On September 24, 2013, a witness having lunch with their family observed a very bright ball of light passing silently over a line of trees in a straight line, then appearing to zigzag very quickly and change direction. Given the elements defined in the investigation report—namely, a very bright, bright ball of light, moving in a straight line at the beginning and end of its trajectory, consistent with a wind-borne object, and with a change of direction consistent with variable winds in the area, as well as the possibility of thunderstorm activity that could produce ball lightning—we have two plausible, but rather unlikely, hypotheses. The information provided by the witnesses does not allow us to confirm or rule out these hypotheses. This case is classified as C due to a lack of information and corroboration.

summary: Long successive observations of the evolution of a luminous and silent phenomenon in the sky: probable observations of luminous animations.
description: On Tuesday, September 24, 2013, between 10:00 and 11:00 PM, two people observed a rapidly changing luminous phenomenon in the sky. Other similar observations were subsequently made from the hamlet. Each time, no unusual noise was heard, and the observations lasted an hour or more. The witness's description of the luminous phenomenon, and the police's confirmation of the observation, strongly suggest the beam of a spotlight coming from the ground. Although there were no nightclubs in the direction of the observation, the police reported that the sparsely populated mountainous area is often the site of informal gatherings (raves). The photograph taken by the witness, which contains a bright circle, does not actually show the observed phenomenon: this bright circle at the top of the image is an "orb" caused by the camera flash striking a speck of dust very close to the lens. See: Circular light spots or orbs. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of light animation. GEIPAN did not investigate the source of the projector, an extremely difficult task given that these installations are temporary and often clandestine.

summary: Three successive observations of the movement of shapes with non-flashing colored lights: lack of information.
description: motorist was intrigued by three successive sightings on September 23rd around 8:30 PM. Exiting the A20 motorway, the witness described a large triangular shape with three lights (red, yellow, and blue) at each end. A little further on, she observed another similar shape, this time more distant. Finally, around a bend, she saw a luminous, potato-shaped mass flying low and slowly, surrounded by small triangles. No other witness statements were collected. This case is based on three sightings by a single witness during a car journey of about ten kilometers. The witness's stress visibly increased during her account. The second and third sightings may therefore have been influenced by the first UFO sighting, which greatly impressed the witness. All three sightings could be the subject of plausible explanations, but none of them could be proven (see the investigation report). The strangeness of this case can therefore be estimated at 0.5. The consistency of the account is weak: the observer was isolated at the time of her report, even though she encountered other vehicles that did not appear surprised by the UFO, which also astonished the witness. She was very emotional about these observations during the interview, which may have affected the accuracy of her account. Furthermore, certain inconsistencies in the account (presence of the Moon) weaken the consistency of the UFO, assessed at 0.5. In conclusion, based on these elements, GEIPAN classifies this case in category C, due to a lack of verifiable information and corroboration.

summary: Observation of the movement of a bright point in the sky: mistaken for an airplane contrail.
description: On September 23, 2013, between 8:10 PM and 8:25 PM, a driver on the D650 between Les Mézières and Saint-Germain-sur-Ay (beach) was intrigued by two bright points in the sky. One point in particular appeared to follow a straight trajectory and move away at a constant speed to the northwest. The witness clearly identified an airplane with its contrail crossing their field of vision. The witness stopped at two locations to take several photographs of the bright point. The witness's testimony and the very high-quality photographs clearly suggest the observation of a distant airplane contrail moving away from the witness. Upon zooming in on the last photos, the bright point appears to have a flame-like shape, which is a perspective view of an airplane contrail brightly illuminated by the setting sun (sunset at 7:54 PM). The reconstructions performed with FlightRadar24 (attached) show that one, and even two, candidate aircraft could have caused these contrails. (Note: the witness's estimated direction of observation is not precise enough to be certain that these are the aircraft. Furthermore, FlightRadar24 only indicates civilian aircraft equipped with a specific type of equipment.) See other similar cases on aircraft contrails. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," a very probable observation of aircraft condensation trails at sunset.

summary: Observation of a silvery spherical shape becoming white, bright and elongated, seemingly motionless, then splitting in two and disappearing instantly: observation of the reflection of the sun on an airplane.
description: On Sunday, September 22, 2013, at 6:45 PM, several people in cars were intrigued by the sight of an unexplained phenomenon in the sky. The witness, in the car, described a silvery spherical shape that became a bright, elongated white shape, seemingly motionless, then splitting in two and disappearing. The radar scan (see diagram) clearly shows the aircraft at high altitude (black trail) described by the witness, and also, at low altitude (therefore without a contrail), an aircraft moving away from the witness (red trail). The aircraft, moving away from the witness almost directly in line with the observation, appeared motionless. When the aircraft changed direction at 6:50 PM (see top right of the diagram, leftward turn from 6:48 PM to 6:51 PM), the reflection changed and disappeared, suggesting that the object itself had vanished. (Note: the times indicated along the contrails are in Universal Time). The witness's initial intuition—sunlight reflecting off an aircraft—ultimately proved to be the correct explanation. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": perfectly explained by sunlight reflecting off an aircraft.

summary: Successive observations of luminous phenomena in the sky: astronomical observations of Venus and the passage of a bolide.
description: witness reports successive observations of silent, luminous spheres in the sky between the evenings of September 22nd and 28th, 2013. This account of sightings of a very bright sphere near the horizon, visible for a long time and for several consecutive days, and seemingly following the observer, is a classic case of mistaken identity, sometimes called a "following sphere." Its origin is obviously astronomical: in this case, it is the planet Venus, bright this autumn in the early evening (Magnitude = -4.7). The direction indicated by the witness on their drawing corresponds to an approximate azimuth of 241°, while Venus is at the same time at an azimuth of 235°. The photos are entirely consistent with this hypothesis, and the witness also points out another, less luminous, orange sphere slightly above and to the right, which is the planet Saturn (see astronomical chart). The witness reported a very different phenomenon on September 23, 2013: the observation, lasting only a few seconds, of a very rapid passage of an orange ball. This much rarer phenomenon, called a bolide, most likely corresponds to the reentry of a meteoroid (meteorite) into the atmosphere. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": observation of Venus and a bolide.

summary: Observation of the movement of several luminous orange balls: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: Recent testimony of an old observation. The witness observed several orange orbs moving at low altitude in the sky, which then went out one after the other. The observation of orange orbs moving slowly in the sky for a few minutes, on a Saturday night into Sunday morning, strongly suggests Thai lanterns, probably licked after a celebration. GEIPAN was unable to verify that these orbs were indeed moving with the wind, as the testimony was too imprecise. GEIPAN classifies this somewhat unusual testimony in category "B": probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of a red, cylindrical object passing across the sky: observation of a passenger plane at sunrise.
description: On Sunday, September 22, 2013, at 7:45 a.m., a witness walking to work was intrigued by the presence in the sky of a very thin, elongated cylinder, moving faster than a previously seen aircraft. The object disappeared into the southwest. Given the details described in the report—namely, the altitude and azimuth of the unidentified flying object (UFO) being consistent with those of aircraft present in the area at the time of the observation, and its appearance resembling that of an aircraft illuminated by the rising sun—we can conclude that the UFO observed by the witness was probably a passenger plane flying at a medium altitude and illuminated by the rising sun. This testimony is quite consistent: fairly precise, but coming from a single witness and without a photograph. The observation is not particularly strange; the UFO was simply observed under specific, easily explainable conditions. This case is classified as B as observation of a passenger plane at sunrise: the testimony is not precise enough to be able to identify exactly the plane observed, among the multiplicity of planes at that time.

summary: Observation of a light followed by the passage of a dark mass above the vehicle: lack of information.
description: On September 15, 2013, at 4:00 AM, a motorist intermittently observed a light in the sky, followed by the passage of a dark, oval mass with "small, integrated luminous discs" above her vehicle. No other witness statements were collected. The witness reported the observation again in May 2014. Considering the available evidence: - The appearance was not consistent with that of a helicopter. - The appearance was initially consistent with nightclub lasers (given the date, which was Saturday to Sunday), but there is no evidence to confirm this hypothesis. We can conclude that the UFO observed by the witness is of unknown nature and origin. This case is classified as C due to a lack of information to verify hypotheses that are fairly consistent with the observation. This testimony is quite consistent: fairly precise, but coming from a single witness and without a photograph. The observation is strange because it is a phenomenon with an unusual appearance, although its movement itself is common.

summary: Successive observations of ballets of luminous white circles in the sky: observation of a luminous animation of the "sky tracer" type.
description: On Saturday, September 14, 2013, between 11:45 PM and midnight, two witnesses were intrigued by successive displays of bright white circles in the sky. No noise was heard during the observations. The appearance of the phenomenon strongly suggests a "sky tracer," a light projection system used for festive events and nightclubs. A nightclub in Pézenas confirmed that it had exceptionally used one of these systems that evening for a special event. It should be noted that the witnesses saw the phenomenon to the south, and that the Montpellier weather report indicated cloudy skies for that evening, conducive to beautiful effects from this system. This case is classified as "A": confirmed observation of a "sky tracer" type light display.

summary: Observation of the movement of numerous bright points in the sky in a group: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: In the early hours of September 8, 2013, at 1:25 a.m., a couple observed about thirty whitish lights moving east-west in the sky. Their speed was constant, and no noise, trails, or flashing lights were observed. The sighting of dozens of lights flying together in a straight line on Saturday night/Sunday morning is quite common and strongly suggests Thai lanterns, likely released after a wedding. The witness observed the lights 800 meters from the Château Saint-Aignan, which had hosted a wedding reception that evening. It was not possible to correlate the direction of movement with the wind recorded in Bordeaux-Mérignac at that time, as the very light wind changed direction at least every hour, and the proximity of the Dordogne River could have caused local breezes. GEIPAN classified this case as 'B': probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of five red lights in the sky: observation of Thai lanterns being licked during a private party.
description: On Sunday, September 8, 2013, at 4:19 a.m., two people were intrigued by the successive appearance in the sky of several very bright red lights moving silently in the same direction. A witness filmed their observation and posted it on a dedicated website. This sighting was the subject of a field investigation by investigators commissioned by GEIPAN. The time, the video, the wind direction, witness statements, and measurements all confirmed that these were indeed sky lanterns. The location of the licking was found, but not without difficulty (see the investigation report). The witnesses acted in good faith but misinterpreted the event, initially dismissing the lantern explanation based on their internet research. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A," perfectly explained by the observation of Thai lanterns being licked during a private party.

summary: Observation of the rectilinear movement in the sky of a white cylindrical object: probable observation of a balloon.
description: On Saturday, September 7, 2013, between 1:10 PM and 1:40 PM, a motorist driving northeast towards Poissy (78) observed a long white cylinder 15° above the horizon. He saw this cylinder move away in a straight line and then disappear in the direction of Poissy (78). No other reports were collected. The Météociel weather report indicated a southwest wind at Toussus-le-Noble (southeast of Poissy) and a west wind at Pontoise. A southwest to west wind can be estimated at Poissy. The observation is consistent with a cylindrical balloon carried by the wind: the cylindrical shape suggests a thermal balloon (solar balloon) launched from Orgeval or Feucherolles, or even much further away, since these balloons can fly for hours. (Note that the Associations Forum was held in Orgeval and Feucherolles that day). These balloons are often dark gray or transparent; the white color may be the result of sunlight reflecting off the object, almost at its zenith. GEIPAN classifies this ultimately rather unusual observation as "B," suggesting it is likely a balloon.
