The low level of strangeness of the case does not warrant a field investigation, which is too unpredictable in urban areas for this type of phenomenon.

summary: Very short observation of the evolution of several white luminous phenomena in the cloudy sky: lack of information.
description: On September 9, 2013, at 10:02 PM or 10:03 PM, a witness observed several white luminous phenomena moving silently across the cloudy sky for five seconds. These phenomena appeared to move in a linear fashion, then rotate counterclockwise, before disappearing. Only one witness account was recorded. The white circles, seemingly projected onto the clouds and rotating in a circular motion, resembled the animation projectors used in nightclubs. Friday evenings at 10:00 PM are typical for this type of promotion; however, there do not appear to be any nightclubs within 10 km of the observation site (there are some in the suburbs of Bordeaux, 12 km away, and others near Blaye, 18 km away, which is too far for the projections to be easily visible). Despite the strong similarity to the effect of a 'skyrose' type projector, but lacking any other testimony, and due to a lack of cross-checking, GEIPAN classifies this case as C: lack of information.

summary: Observation of a succession of bright white flashes: probable observation of flashes coming from an electric locomotive.
description: On September 5, 2013, at 4:29 a.m., a witness, during a break at work, sat down outside a building. He was then startled by a series of five powerful white flashes, which he observed coming from a nearby GSM relay antenna. No unusual noise was heard. No other witness statements were collected. After a field investigation with the witness, the GEIPAN investigator carefully analyzed several hypotheses: the illumination of the cloud layer by flashes produced by the pantograph(s) of a passing train on the curved railway line, located 2,500 meters along the observer's line of sight, seemed to account for almost all of the characteristics described by the witness. GEIPAN classifies this case as B: probable observation of flashes from an electric locomotive.

summary: Successive observations of luminous phenomena in the sky during the same evening: lack of information.
description: On September 4, 2013, starting at 11:45 PM, two witnesses observing the sky were intrigued by round, luminous phenomena of varying colors that they could not explain. In total, between 2 and 30 phenomena were observed. Only one witness statement was recorded. This complex statement lacked detail, given the lengthy observation period (approximately one hour). The witness, contacted by telephone on February 24, 2014, announced that the other witness would also send their observation report, but GEIPAN (the French National Gendarmerie's Office for the Study of Astronomical Phenomena) had still not received it by November 2014. This case is classified as "C" due to a lack of information, pending further witness statements.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of a round or oblong object (depending on the angles) of matte dark color in the sky: probable observation of an autogyro.
description: On September 2, 2013, at 12:45 PM, a witness was intrigued by the silent movement of an object in the sky. It made a few preliminary turns and appeared round and oblong depending on the viewing angle during these initial maneuvers. Given the information available in the investigation report—namely, the presence of a nearby airfield offering autogyro flights, the absence of non-mandatory lights on autogyros, the compatible shape and color, and the largely consistent movements and speeds—we can conclude that the UFO observed by the witness was probably an autogyro in its climbing phase. This testimony is of average quality: rather imprecise with numerous inaccuracies, coming from a single witness and without a photograph. The observation is not particularly unusual, as it could have been a completely ordinary object. This case is classified as a probable autogyro sighting (B).

summary: Observation of a very bright point in the sky with variation in intensity and movement: mistaken for a flash from the Iridium 95 satellite.
description: On August 31, 2013, at approximately 11:30 PM, a witness observed a very bright white point among the stars from their doorstep. During the observation, the witness noted that the brightness varied (increasing then decreasing) and that the object moved in a straight upward line before disappearing from view. Only one witness statement was recorded. Of low strangeness and moderate consistency (a single witness but a fairly precise account), this case turned out to be the observation of a rare but well-known astronautical phenomenon: a reflection of the sun on the Iridium 95 satellite, called a flash or flare (see the investigation report and Iridium Satellite Flashes?). This case is classified as Class A, mistaken for a flash from the Iridium 95 satellite.

summary: Observation of bursts of white light in the constellation Pegasus: probable mistaking for a very high-altitude satellite in rapid rotation.
description: On August 31, 2013, between 10:40 PM and 11:00 PM, an amateur astronomer, observing the sky with two friends from Chalmazel (42), noticed flashes of white light in the constellation Pegasus. Two other people witnessed the UFO but could not be interviewed. Of low strangeness and medium consistency (several witnesses, but only one account), this case appears to be a probable misidentification of a very high-altitude, rapidly rotating satellite (see investigation notes). Furthermore, at least seven very high-altitude satellites were present in the observation area during the time interval given by the witness. The witness's visual perception was not the issue, but rather their interpretation of the observation based on their feelings (surprise, observation of only four short flashes). This case is classified as Class B, probable misidentification of a very high-altitude, rapidly rotating satellite.

summary: Observation of the S-shaped movement of a multicolored point in the night sky: lack of information.
description: On August 30, 2013, at approximately 10:30 PM, a witness observed a blue point, about the size of a tennis ball, silently descending from the sky for about ten seconds, following an S-shaped trajectory. During its descent, the colors changed from blue to red, then to green, and finally to yellow. The light suddenly went out. Given the available information, in particular: - no precise details on the UFO's trajectory; - no precise details on the UFO's luminous or colorimetric characteristics; - no angular measurements; we can conclude that the lack of information prevents us from favoring any hypothesis. This case is classified as C, meaning it is an observation of a phenomenon that cannot be identified in its current state, as the significant lack of information prevents us from establishing a firm opinion. This testimony is of weak substance: although a sketch exists, it remains imprecise and lacking in detail, and also lacks crucial data necessary for the continuation of the study. There is only one eyewitness account and no photographic or video documentation. The observation could be moderately strange; however, too many inaccuracies and gaps in the testimony prevent a truly valid assessment of its strangeness.

summary: Presence of an object in a photograph without direct observation: probable photograph of a satellite flare.
description: The witness, wanting to photograph a star trail, adjusted his camera accordingly. The next day, he saw that he had captured a luminous object that remained stable, unlike the other stars, which had moved during the 5-minute exposure time between shots. A bright spot in a long-exposure astronomy photograph more likely reveals a brief luminous event than a phenomenon that remained stationary during the 5-minute exposure. This bright spot, moreover, turned out to be a small streak, indicating partial movement during the 5-minute exposure. The leading hypothesis is the reflection of the sun on a satellite: the attached "Calsky" report indicates that the NOSS 3-3A and 3C satellites were passing through the camera's field of view at that moment, culminating at 27 arcseconds above the horizon (it would appear that the spot in the photograph is slightly higher). It appears that the satellite NOSS 3-3C (28541) see: Satflare NOSS3-3C may have a stronger and more variable brightness than NOSS3-3A (28537) see: Satflare NOSS3-3A. The small black line observed below the white line when zooming in on the photo is probably a side effect of JPEG compression (the white line "bounces"—it's a shame the photos weren't taken in RAW). In the attached Pleiades photo, greatly enlarged, you can see that each star image is surrounded by a black line: this is the same compression artifact. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable photograph of a satellite flare. (There remains some uncertainty about the satellite that caused the flare).

summary: Observation of two luminous balls near the setting sun: certain observation of a parhelion.
description: On August 29, 2013, at 7:45 PM, a motorist was surprised to observe two luminous phenomena not far from sunset. He took the time to stop and photograph the phenomenon. This account is very consistent: precise and with five usable photos. Considering the elements of the investigation, namely: - appearance and color of the UFOs; - low sun on the horizon and UFOs at the same altitude; - presence of clouds conducive to the formation of parhelions, we can conclude that the UFO observed by the witnesses is very likely a parhelion phenomenon. The observation is ultimately quite plausible, as the objects are easily explained and their presence demonstrable. This case is classified as A, indicating a confirmed observation of a parhelion.

summary: Observation of the movement of two luminous phenomena in the sky: lack of information.
description: On Sunday, August 25, 2013, between 7:30 and 7:45 PM, a witness observed two successive luminous phenomena in the sky from their balcony, which they could not identify. The observation of a large red light in the sky for two minutes, moving slowly, could have been a Thai lantern moving with the wind towards the witness (the prevailing easterly wind on Réunion Island). The bright white light, a sign of the wind from the sea, could have been a satellite: the Calsky forecast (attached) indicates the passage of the satellite "USA 217/STPSat-2" on a compatible trajectory at the given time; however, the brightness reported by the witness is not consistent with the low brightness predicted by the Calsky model (magnitude between 5 and 8), but a reflection cannot be ruled out. It could also have been another, unlisted, and brighter military satellite. These two hypotheses, while plausible, are not sufficiently substantiated for GEIPAN to consider them highly probable. GEIPAN classifies this somewhat unusual observation as case "C" due to a lack of information to support these hypotheses.

summary: Observation of spheres at night and in a photograph: lack of information.
description: On Saturday, August 24, 2013, at 10:00 PM, while taking photographs, witnesses were intrigued by the presence of a sphere to the left of the Moon. The witness took a photo and later noticed a second sphere. In the witness's photo, the Moon is clearly visible: a small, white, gibbous disk (see Stellarium map). The two large luminous disks to the left are photographic artifacts, sometimes called "orbs," created by dust or water droplets very close to the lens and illuminated by the flash. This does not explain the second large luminous sphere observed by the witness to the left of the Moon: a lunar halo? A stadium lamppost (see Google image)? Some other phenomenon? Due to this uncertainty and the lack of evidence provided by the photograph, GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" due to insufficient information.

summary: Prolonged observation of the silent presence of a luminous ball in the sky: probable observation of a weather balloon.
description: On Wednesday, August 21, 2013, at 9:46 a.m., a walker was intrigued by a bright light in the clear sky above the sea. The brightness gradually decreased before disappearing. The observation lasted between 20 and 25 minutes. No other reports were collected about this bright and silent phenomenon. Astronomical conditions: Sun: azimuth: 104°, elevation: 32°. Atmospheric conditions: Sustained northwest wind: 19 to 28 km/h, and clear skies. The observation, at the beginning or end of the day, for 20 minutes, of a nearly stationary point of light in the sky strongly suggests a high-altitude balloon. GEIPAN was unable to verify this hypothesis, which nevertheless corresponds well to the observation. There are no regular weather balloon launches from Nice or the surrounding area, but several scientific institutes are likely to launch them in the Southeast region or in Italy. Modeling the movement of a high-altitude balloon is extremely complex because high-altitude winds, often very powerful, differ from ground-level winds. GEIPAN classifies this somewhat unusual observation as "B," suggesting it is probably a weather balloon.

summary: Observation in flight of an ovoid and yellow object moving at high speed: lack of information.
description: The witness, a Cessna 150 pilot flying southwest of Metz (on a flight from Colmar to Liège), observed a small, yellow, ovoid-shaped object moving at high speed to the northwest, at the same altitude, from north to south. The duration of the observation is not specified. Since the distance of an unknown object cannot be estimated, the observer's estimated altitude is uncertain: it could be a very bright and distant object at a higher altitude, in which case it would be an atmospheric reentry of a meteorite or space debris. Space-Track catalogs of space debris reentries do not record any reentries on that day. As the observation occurred during daylight hours, a reflection of the sun on another aircraft is also a possibility. Lacking information to support either of these hypotheses, GEIPAN classifies this case as "C".

summary: Observation of the movement of an orange luminous phenomenon in the sky: probable observation of a Thai lantern.
description: On August 20, 2013, at 10:40 PM, three people observed the silent passage of an orange light across the sky. The sighting of an orange ball moving silently across the sky suggested a Thai lantern. Weather reports from Grenoble and Lyon indicated a strong northerly wind. This wind was consistent with the observed movement from northwest to southeast. The video perfectly supports this hypothesis. These lanterns are more often released on weekends, but weekday events during the summer are not uncommon (Tuesday in this case). This observation, which is quite plausible, is classified as "B" as a probable Thai lantern sighting.

summary: Observation of a sudden and intense luminous phenomenon in the sky: observation of the flash of an Iridium satellite.
description: On August 19, 2013, at approximately 11:00 PM, a witness observed a star that appeared to enter the atmosphere before stopping, illuminating the sky, and then moving in the opposite direction of its initial trajectory. Given the objective evidence gathered (see the investigation report), namely: - exceptional brightness; - a color identical to that of a satellite; - visibility from the witness's location; - the time of visibility coinciding with the presence of the Iridium 49 satellite, we can conclude that the witness's observation was that of an Iridium flare produced by the Iridium 49e satellite. This phenomenon is caused by the reflection of sunlight on the satellite's particularly large antenna. The flare is so bright that it is even visible in broad daylight. This case is classified as an A-level observation of an Iridium satellite flare.

summary: Observations of the silent and straight passage of a group of about ten orange objects forming a luminous triangle in the sky: observations of Thai lanterns.
description: On August 18, 2013, around 2:00 AM, three witnesses were intrigued by the straight and silent passage of a luminous phenomenon across the sky. Up to 11 yellow-orange discs were counted, forming a moving triangular shape. The phenomenon moved away and disappeared into the landscape. This was certainly a lantern sighting; all the characteristics were present: color, absence of noise, and the characteristic formation of licks in clusters. Furthermore, the venue where a wedding was held was located approximately 400 meters from the observation point, so the lanterns were likely still at a low altitude and very close to one another when the witnesses saw them, reinforcing the impression of a single structure. The almost complete absence of wind allowed these lanterns to move slowly and in a straight line above the witnesses. Furthermore, confirmations from the town hall and then from the person who rented the wedding venue leave no doubt about the lantern release at the time of observation. This case is classified as A: confirmed sightings of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the silent and rectilinear movement of a light in the sky: observation of the passage of the International Space Station (ISS).
description: On August 17, 2013, around 11:00 PM, two people were intrigued by the presence of a very bright light moving silently across the sky in a straight line. The description of the phenomenon perfectly matches the observation of the International Space Station. The record of passes of this station (source: Calsky.com) indicates that it was clearly visible that evening from Pontarlier at 11:15 PM, which corresponds to the time indicated by the witness (approximate time, according to the witness). GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": ISS observation.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of a grey-metallic object in the sky: probable observation of a balloon of unknown origin.
description: On August 16, 2013, at 1:33 PM, three people were intrigued by the silent passage of a gray-metallic object across the sky. Only one witness account was recorded. According to the witness, who was observing in the direction of the "Baou" (the Baou des Blancs summit) located west of La Gaude, he saw the object flying from his left to his right, therefore from south to north; he saw it rise. The observation lasted approximately four minutes. This direction of movement is consistent with the south wind blowing at approximately 18 km/h. If it was a wind-borne object, it would have traveled a little over 1 km. If we assume a 2-meter balloon (e.g., a homemade solar balloon Solar Balloon Flight), the geometric analysis of the photo places it at approximately 700 meters (see diagram). It could also be 4 meters in diameter and 1.4 km away. The origin of this balloon could not be determined by GEIPAN: no notable celebrations in the southern vicinity of the witness. It could be an experimental object made by an amateur, or a celebratory object (one could imagine the shape of a "1"). GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of a balloon of unknown origin.

summary: Observation of the rectilinear movement of a bright light in the sky: re-entry into the atmosphere of a fragment of an asteroid (meteoroid) or of a satellite debris.
description: This account describes fixed points of light in the sky every night, without further details. It also mentions a brief luminous phenomenon on August 13, 2013; only this latter phenomenon was considered, due to a lack of precise information about the former, which were most likely related to stars. A bright light moving at high speed across the sky for two seconds strongly suggests a fireball, that is, the entry into the atmosphere of a fragment of an asteroid (meteoroid) or a piece of satellite debris. An automatic camera belonging to the BOAM meteor observer network is located in May-sur-Orne, about 65 km from the site of this observation. It recorded numerous fireballs that night, during the Perseid meteor shower. Three fireballs corresponding approximately to the observation were found within a 5-minute window around the declared observation time (2:35 local time). GEIPAN classifies this observation as "A": fireball, meaning the re-entry into the atmosphere of a fragment of an asteroid (meteoroid) or a piece of satellite debris.

summary: Observation of the passage of a bright point in the sky of varying intensity: satellite reflection phenomenon, involving the former satellite Cosmos 2268.
description: On August 13, 2013, at approximately 8:00 PM, a witness observed a bright point in the sky moving along a straight trajectory. Its speed was slow and its magnitude constant. The object began to shine with great intensity. While of moderate strangeness, but with sufficient consistency (numerous coherent and precise details lending credibility to the case), this event turned out to be a classic case of mistaken identity involving a satellite reflection phenomenon. Further investigation identified the satellite most likely responsible for this misinterpretation: the Russian military satellite COSMOS 2268, a Strela3 type satellite. After further investigation, the witness himself validated and confirmed this hypothesis. This case is classified as Class A: satellite reflection phenomenon involving the former Cosmos 2268 satellite.

summary: Observation of the movements of three luminous balls in the clear sky: observation of the passage of Thai lanterns.
description: On August 12, 2013, at 12:08 AM, a family observed the silent movement of three very bright orbs: the first two followed a linear trajectory and then rose into the clear sky, while the third moved above the houses, changing color. All three phenomena disappeared simultaneously. This sighting of luminous orange or colored orbs moving slowly across the sky clearly corresponds to the observation of Thai lanterns. The day's weather report indicated a light, variable wind, blowing mainly from the southwest at the time of the observation, which corresponds to the overall eastward movement observed. This irregular movement is not surprising in light winds in an urban coastal area, due to the complexity of the various air currents originating from urban, thermal, or marine sources. The video posted some time ago on YouTube was entirely consistent with this hypothesis. The tourist location, the summer period, and the time of day are perfectly suited to lantern licking during festivals. The witness is not convinced by this hypothesis. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Night observation of a strong light on a mountainside: very likely observation of a powerful flashlight.
description: On August 12, 2013, between approximately 11:15 PM and 11:33 PM, a witness observed a bright light flickering slowly and irregularly on a mountainside. It was located near a very difficult-to-access area, which surprised the witness. The phenomenon diminished in intensity and disappeared. Given the elements of the investigation file, namely that the observation area is a zone of human activity (access to the Valmenier chairlifts) and that the color and appearance of the unidentified flying object (UFO) are typical of the use of a flashlight, we can conclude that the UFO observed by the witness was very likely a powerful flashlight used by one or more people present at the location, near the chairlift facilities. This case is classified as Category B, as a very probable observation of a powerful flashlight.

summary: Observation of the slow passage of several orange lights in the sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On August 11, 2013, around midnight, a witness observed several orange objects in the clear sky, distinct from the stars. Their east-southeast movement was slow, and the witness took several photographs. The witness's description is entirely consistent with the observation of Thai lanterns, quite common on summer nights in cities: round orange lights flying continuously. The objects were moving towards the east-southeast: the weather report for Quimper indicated a light westerly wind, generally consistent with the movement of objects carried by the wind. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Long observation of the presence of a white luminous point which appears static, followed by two white trails forming a baseless triangle: certain observation of a passenger plane with short condensation trails.
description: On the A62 motorway between Agen and Toulouse, on August 11, 2013, around 7:00 AM, a driver and his passenger observed for about twenty minutes the presence of a white light that appeared stationary, followed by two white trails forming a baseless triangle in the northeast sky. The car eventually passed the phenomenon, and the witnesses lost sight of the UFO. Only one witness statement was collected. This statement was fairly consistent: precise but without photographs or videos. The observation was quite ordinary; it was an object with ultimately commonplace behavior and appearance. Given the elements defined in the investigation report (see document), namely the meteorological conditions conducive to the formation or absence of condensation at high altitude, as well as the appearance being consistent with similar photographic cases occurring under the same conditions, this case is classified as Ae. It is a confirmed sighting of a passenger plane with short condensation trails.

summary: Observations in the sky of rapid movements of an elongated object of metallic color and dark wings: lack of information.
description: On Saturday, August 10, 2013, around 7:30 p.m., several people were intrigued by the silent passage of a dark, cigar-shaped object across the sky. It flew in the wind and moved quite quickly just below the clouds. The intermittent observation lasted 15 to 20 seconds. The eyewitness accounts were very precise, and the witnesses were very reliable. The strangeness of the phenomenon was moderate. Indeed, while no hypothesis could explain it based on the specific details reported by the witnesses, the phenomenon could have been an airplane or a drone if the viewing conditions prevented the witnesses from seeing certain characteristic features, or it could have been an object carried by the wind (a balloon shaped like an airplane). The evidence gathered during the investigation did not allow for a definitive or even approximate identification of the phenomenon, which remains moderately strange. Based on the current state of available information, this case is classified as category C, due to a lack of precise information on distance and wind estimation.

summary: Observation of the passage of a light grey triangular object across the sky: lack of information.
description: On August 9, 2013, at midnight, several people were watching shooting stars and were surprised to see a light gray, triangular object moving NE-SW at low altitude and without noise. Only one brief eyewitness account was collected. This account is of very little substance: imprecise and lacking in detail, and also lacking essential data necessary for the continuation of the study. The eyewitness is unique and there are no photographic or video documentation. The observation could be considered moderately strange; however, too many inaccuracies and gaps in the account prevent a truly valid assessment of its strangeness. Given the elements defined in the attached investigation report, GEIPAN classifies this case as C due to lack of information.

summary: Observation of the movement of two flashing bright points: probable observation of the passage of two military satellites.
description: On August 8, 2013, a witness at a summer camp was observing the sky with a friend. He recounted one of his observations, during which, around 10:30 PM, he saw two bright points in the sky moving along a straight path while blinking. This very detailed observation report clearly suggests the sighting of satellites. Consulting the Calsky website allows us to consider two hypotheses: - The ISS passing overhead at 10:27 PM: however, the International Space Station is much brighter than the stars, making it difficult to explain the two bright points. The ISS passed south of Polaris, while the witness described the objects to the north. - The two military satellites NOSS 2-1B and 1C passing overhead at 10:37 PM. These satellites are less bright, but could reflect sunlight irregularly and produce the effect described by the witness. Their trajectory corresponds very well to the witness's observation. This is the hypothesis that GEIPAN is considering, despite a 7-minute discrepancy compared to the testimony.

summary: Two sightings of a dark, rectangular shape with red and white lights passing by: very likely sighting of a military cargo plane.
description: On August 8, 2013, at approximately 11:10-11:15 PM, two people in an apartment noticed a fairly loud and constant noise and observed a dark, rectangular object flying at low altitude. They did not recognize the object. Red and white lights were also seen. Based on the information gathered—namely, the lights, the distance and size consistent with a military cargo plane, the typical noise of such an aircraft, the gray color, the indefinable shape against the night sky, the corresponding flight path, and the fact that the aircraft had previously flown on it—we can conclude that the unidentified flying object (UFO) observed by the witnesses was very likely a military cargo plane, an A400M, approaching the Velizy-Villacoublay airfield. This testimony is very consistent: two witnesses gave detailed statements to the Gendarmerie and GEIPAN (the French National Gendarmerie Intervention Group), each accompanied by a sketch; however, there are no photographic or video documents. The observation is ultimately not very strange, as it involves a fairly common object observed under unusual, and therefore infrequent, circumstances. This case should be classified as B, a highly probable sighting of a military cargo plane.

summary: Observation of the displacement OE of a point of light in the sky: observation of the passage of the ISS.
description: On August 5, 2013, at 11:14 PM, a couple observed a very bright point of light in the sky. This observation of a very bright point crossing the sky from west to east at the beginning of the night had all the characteristics of observing a large satellite: the International Space Station (ISS) passed overhead that evening, precisely at that time: from 11:11 PM to 11:16 PM (see the Calsky report). The fact that the witness indicated that the light "at times seemed to deviate from its trajectory" is probably the result of a visual illusion: see perception of the movement of a bright point in the sky. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": observation of the ISS passing overhead.

summary: Observation of several yellowish lights grouped together in the sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On August 5, 2013, between 11:00 PM and 11:20 PM, a witness observed five yellowish lights in the stormy sky, appearing to flicker. Their movement was rapid. The lights veered to the left and disappeared from the witness's view. A few seconds later, another light appeared and followed the same path. This testimony is of high quality, accurately describing the positions of the observed objects. The witness's description is entirely consistent with the observation of Thai lanterns, quite common on summer nights in cities: orange balls flying continuously. The objects, observed to the south-southeast, moved eastward. However, the wind direction, from the northwest, does not exactly match the observed path; one might consider local disturbances due to the nearby Moselle River and the Plappeville hill just to the west of the witness. Wind speeds in Metz: Northwest 16 to 30 km/h: weather. This is a "B" case: probable sighting of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the particular movement of lights on the horizon: observation of flight AT514 during the landing phase.
description: On August 5, 2013, at approximately 11:50 PM, several witnesses were intrigued by the silent, north-south movement of five bright lights on the horizon above the sea. Following an investigation by the civil aviation authorities, only one hypothesis was considered: the passage of a long-haul airliner, Air Corsica flight 514 AT from Paris to Bastia. This plane was significantly delayed, as it was scheduled to land at 11:00 PM, but it landed at precisely 12:02 AM at Bastia-Porette Airport, located south of Bastia (meaning it passed over Bastia between 11:40 PM and 11:55 PM). The five white lights seen by witnesses could be the position lights and wingtip lights of this Airbus A320, which shifted in position as the aircraft turned and began its descent to align with the runway. It is possible that the landing lights were activated on approach to the airport, which could have altered the witnesses' perception of the lights. If the observed phenomenon was not flight AT 514, it would have attracted the attention of airport air traffic control, which was on high alert, given that flight AT 514 was the last to approach Bastia-Poretta Airport. The air transport police noticed nothing unusual and reported nothing. No articles appeared in the local press in the following days. We were unable to find any other witnesses to this phenomenon. In conclusion, GEIPAN classifies this case as A: observation of flight AT514 during its landing phase. The witness must have been surprised by the highly unusual observation conditions, on the roof of a building, a few kilometers from the aircraft's landing trajectory.

summary: Observation of a stormy sky and observation of colored luminous streaks on a photograph: mistaking it for a photographic artifact.
description: On August 4, 2013, a very hot night, a witness (estimated time 3 or 4 a.m.) took a photo of distant thunderstorms before going to bed (photo DSCN5593). Later, while asleep, a bright light woke him and his husband; they both thought it was a thunderstorm. The witness went out onto the balcony and took a second photograph. It was then that he noticed a series of bright, white-yellow streaks in the photograph (photo DSCN5594) and was intrigued. What the witnesses saw did not create any particular strangeness. "My wife said, 'Lightning is coming here.' We saw streaks of light that we interpreted as lightning" (see questionnaire). The strangeness and the subject of the testimony seem to stem from what is seen in photo DSCN5594. Analysis of this photo indicates the presence of photographic artifacts, likely caused by the exposure time (8 seconds) and the camera's movement within the field of view of lights, even those of moderate intensity, present nearby before the end of the exposure. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies this case as A: misinterpretation with a photographic artifact.

summary: Observation of a bright white point of light in the night sky and questioning the zoomed-in photograph: observation of a satellite passing overhead
description: On August 4, 2013, at 10:12 PM, a couple observed a white point of light moving at the same speed as a passenger jet, but without flashing, in a straight line, without making any noise. The witness took two photos with a camera and was surprised by what he obtained when zooming in on his computer (see photo 3). Only one witness statement was collected. The strangeness that prompted the witness's statement stemmed from what he saw in the photo and not from what he saw with his own eyes, which he himself admitted was probably a satellite. Indeed, at the time indicated, several satellites passed overhead in a SW to NE direction (see Callsky). GEIPAN no longer considers (due to the numerous photographic artifacts) strange phenomena resulting from photographs that were not seen with the naked eye and is only commenting on the visual aspect. GEIPAN classifies the case as A: observation of a satellite's passage.

summary: Observation of the silent and rapid movement of an orange ball in the sky: probable observation of the passage of a Thai lantern.
description: On Friday, August 2, 2013, around midnight, a family in a car was intrigued by the silent and rapid movement of a bright orange ball in the clear sky. The object disappeared, hidden by the landscape. Observing an orange ball moving in a straight line on a weekend evening suggests a Thai lantern. At that moment, a south wind of 19 km/h was recorded in Méco: weather. The witness was surprised by the speed of the phenomenon: if a lantern truly flies at 19 km/h in a straight line, it can be difficult to follow it by car. The case is classified as "B": probable observation of a Thai lantern.

summary: Observation from a car of the presence of four red-orange lights in the clear sky; successive extinction of the lights: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On August 2, 2013, at 11:08 PM, a witness and his wife, driving a car (see map), observed four bright red-orange lights in the clear sky, which then faded out one after the other. The Meteociel weather report indicated a light westerly wind. The observation of these lights in the sky for a few minutes on a Saturday evening strongly suggests Thai lanterns. Given the location, the objects were slowly moving eastward from the witnesses. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the silent passage of an orange ball across the sky: lack of information.
description: On August 1, 2013, at 12:40 AM, two people were intrigued by the presence of a flashing orange ball above a tree. The ball then rose into the clear sky and was hidden by a nearby building. No unusual noise was heard. Only one witness statement was recorded. The witness's description perfectly matches the observation of a Thai lantern, a fairly common sight on summer nights in the city: an orange ball moving continuously from west to east across the sky, dimming at the end. However, the wind direction, from the north, and therefore perpendicular to the observed path, does not support this hypothesis. The wind was very light (1 to 4 km/h), suggesting a local breeze with a different direction. Due to a lack of very local meteorological information, this case is classified as "C" for lack of details.

summary: Observation of the slow movement of a luminous ball emitting flashes at regular intervals: probable observation of a satellite (debris) at high altitude, whose rotation creates periodic flashes.
description: On July 31, 2013, starting at midnight, a witness on the Madone d'Utelle plateau was intrigued by the slow, high-altitude movement of a luminous sphere emitting flashes at regular intervals. Among the many satellites visible on summer evenings, it would seem that the third stage of the rocket that launched the American satellite LAGEOS in 1963 could correspond to this observation. In the Calsky document, the star chart oriented to the northwest, with the Big Dipper on the right, shows a white trail corresponding to the object's path across the sky over 30 minutes. This type of object is almost always rotating: a reflective element of this object can periodically reflect the sun powerfully and create a flash. However, the imprecision regarding the phenomenon's position in the sky prevents us from confirming this hypothesis. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of a satellite (debris) at high altitude, whose rotation creates periodic flashes.

summary: Observation of the movement of a pair of yellow-orange lights: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On July 31, 2013, around 11:00 PM, a family observed the silent movement of a pair of bright yellow-orange lights in the sky. The lights suddenly began to ascend in a straight line. The witness was observing from a small village near the Quiberon peninsula, close to the coast, but looking southeast to south, just above the entrance to the peninsula, on the Carnac side. The weather report indicated a southerly wind that day until 3:00 PM, weakening, becoming very variable until 11:00 PM (south then north), then shifting to the northeast at 11:00 PM, and finally settling towards the east after midnight. (Source: weather The time and place are very conducive to the release of Thai lanterns, often launched in groups. The wind recorded in Vannes is consistent with the direction of movement of the observed phenomenon, which is heading west and rising. The Quiberon tourist airport is noted along the witness's line of sight. The phenomenon described by the witness could also correspond to an airplane seen head-on; however, it would be very surprising if there had been any nighttime activity at this small tourist airport. Once the airplane's headlights were switched off, the witness would have been able to see the airplane's flashing lights. The lantern hypothesis remains much more likely. The stationary phase of the phenomenon may correspond to movement towards the witness by a very local breeze. The rapid ascent of lanterns into the sky is normal; the decrease in brightness is often interpreted as movement away; and an observation period of a few minutes is typical for a lantern. Their launch path may have been obscured by buildings or vegetation. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the passage on a straight and slightly ascending trajectory of two red-orange luminous phenomena: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On July 28, 2013, at 3:20 a.m., two witnesses observed two flattened, circular, red-orange lights from the first floor of their home. They moved across the sky along a slightly upward, straight trajectory. The observation lasted one to two minutes without any unusual noise being heard. Only one witness account was recorded. The observation of several red-orange lights moving together in a straight line on a summer night, from Saturday to Sunday, for two minutes, strongly suggests the sighting of Thai lanterns, likely licked after a celebration (more than 400,000 Thai lanterns are sold annually in France). The weather report for Charleville indicates a light and unstable wind: weather. The weather report shows highly variable wind at this time, which does not fully validate this hypothesis, although it remains compatible with the observation for now. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of a Thames lantern.

summary: Observation of the silent passage of a blinking flying object in the night sky: straight trajectory then curved: lack of information.
description: On July 27, 2013, at 11:47 PM, a couple observed a flashing luminous object in the clear sky. Seen through binoculars, the object was described as round, with regular flashes, and amber in color. No sound was heard. Approaching from the south of Nice, the object moved north and then made a smooth, linear turn west of the city and towards the Var region. Only one witness account was collected. The witness's description had all the characteristics of an aircraft: the multiple flashing lights (collision avoidance and 1 Hz strobes), which were not synchronized, often gave the illusion of flashing twice per second. The trajectory of the phenomenon was consistent with that of an aircraft. GEIPAN (the French National Gendarmerie's Offenses Investigation Group) processed this case too late to verify this hypothesis with radar data. Therefore, and as the witness clearly refutes this airplane hypothesis, GEIPAN classifies this case as C due to lack of information.

summary: Observation of the rectilinear and silent movement of a bright orange point in the sky: probable observation of a Thai lantern.
description: On Saturday, July 27, 2013, at 10:00 PM, two walkers were intrigued by the straight and silent movement of an orange light across the sky. The observation lasted two to three minutes before the object disappeared over the horizon. The following day, the witnesses discovered other people who had seen the phenomenon in the area, but no further reports were collected by GEIPAN (the French National Center for Information and Experimentation on Astronomy). This account of a large orange light is extremely well described; it is not unusual. The color, the linear movement, the time, and the date of the observation are consistent with a Thai lantern. The correlation between the movement and the local wind is uncertain: available weather records from Luxembourg and Metz indicate winds from the south or southwest, respectively, but highly variable, which could potentially explain the object's change of direction. Single Thai lanterns are not uncommon. The apparent "radial" speed of Thai lanterns in average winds is of the same order as that of airplanes. The apparent size and strong brightness reported by the witness are difficult to compare to other lanterns, given the variety of models on the one hand, and the observation conditions on the other. This sighting is consistent with a Thai lantern, but not all the indicators needed to confirm it (wind, numerous lechers) are present. A wedding was recorded in Rehon at 4 PM that day. Based on these indicators and uncertainties, GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable sighting of a Thai lantern.

summary: Observation of the presence and movement of orange balls in the sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On Friday, July 26, 2013, around 11:00 PM, a witness observed an orange ball to the south, which disappeared to the east. He then made another similar observation 15 minutes later. The witness reported seeing the moon in the background of a photograph; however, at 11:00 PM, the moon had not yet risen, and moreover, it was only three-quarters full (rising in the east around 11:15 PM). The gray circle in the photograph is more likely the reflection of the camera flash on a speck of dust. The photos provided to GEIPAN are not in the same format as the originals. The wind recorded by Meteociel in Cambrai was very light, oscillating around the northerly direction during the evening. The witness's description is consistent with the observation of two Thai lanterns licked less than a kilometer south of the witness: the very light wind would have carried the lanterns only slightly, and they would have gone out after a few minutes.

summary: Observation of three bright white points forming an equilateral triangle: probable observation of reflections of the sun on the YAOGAN9 satellite triplet.
description: On July 25, 2013, at 12:05 AM, a witness observed the silent movement of three white lights in the sky, forming an equilateral triangle. A satellite pass simulation using the Calsky.com website indicates that the YAOGAN9 satellite triplet was visible to the witness at the time of observation. These satellites appeared as three lights arranged in an equilateral triangle, separated from each other by an angular distance of approximately 1e, or twice the apparent diameter of the full Moon. These satellites could reflect sunlight for a few seconds (flare). See examples, with very different fields of view, on: Yaogan Satellite Triplet Flare and at the 40th second on the right of the video NOSS Yaogan Triplet Flare? The fact that the witness no longer sees the stars in the center of the triangle is probably a classic perceptual illusion when observing groups of bright points. The witness indicated in their questionnaire that the apparent size of the triangle corresponded to 6 cm at arm's length (approximately 5th to 6th arcseconds), then in a separate message that, on December 5, 2013, at 2:40 AM, "the triangle formed by the middle star of the belt with the two feet is identical in proportion, at the same heading and altitude." This triangle is approximately 8 arcseconds on each side. GEIPAN does not have the means to verify that the reflection of the sun on the satellite actually occurred at that precise moment. The significant difference between the size of the Yaogan triplet (1 arcsecond) and the size reported by the witness (between 5th and 8th arcseconds) is substantial and casts doubt on this hypothesis. Due to the near-perfect coincidence in time and position with the passage of these satellites, despite some inconsistencies with the witness's testimony, GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of reflections of the sun on the YAOGAN9 satellite triplet.

summary: Observation of the movement of three bright points in the clear sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On July 25, 2013, at 3:41 a.m., a worker on break outside a building was intrigued by the presence of three lights in the clear sky. These lights were moving at a constant speed and appeared to form a dark triangle. A building obstructed his view, so the witness moved back and forth between two vantage points, but the lights had disappeared. The observation lasted approximately two minutes. There are several possible explanations for the observation of a triplet of lights in the sky. What makes this case unusual is essentially the low probability of alignment between the witness, the locations where the lights disappeared, and the lunar disk. After a field investigation, it was determined that this observation of three lights moving in unison with the wind direction is consistent with the observation of Thai lanterns. GEIPAN was unable to identify the perpetrators of the lecher. This case is class B: probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the movement of a luminous phenomenon in the sky: probable observation of the passage of a bolide.
description: On July 24, 2013, around midnight, several people observed a luminous phenomenon moving silently across the sky for a few seconds. The observation of a long, very bright trail for a few seconds strongly suggests a bolide (the entry into the atmosphere of a meteoroid, which will become a meteorite if it reaches the ground). GEIPAN and other organizations (IMCCE, Ciel des Hommes, BOAM) received numerous similar reports the previous night, that night, and the following nights, evidence that the Earth is passing through a region of space at this time of year that is quite rich in small bodies (meteorite swarms). Nevertheless, this specific event has not been fully characterized. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B" as a probable bolide observation.

summary: Observation of more than 10 flying objects in the space of 30 minutes, of varied shapes and behaviors: lack of information.
description: On July 24, 2013, at midnight, a witness observed more than 10 flying objects within 30 minutes, exhibiting different shapes and behaviors. No other reports were collected. This unusual account describes numerous seemingly spectacular phenomena with varied behaviors. Given the scale of the phenomenon, it is surprising that there was only one witness, unless they were simply faint lights: one could then consider satellites or shooting stars, which are very numerous and visible at that time of night, at that time of year (see Calsky's report). Two rather spectacular flashes from Iridium satellites were also noted. On the same day, GEIPAN received a report of a fireball sighting (BACHANT (59) 24.07.2013), and numerous witnesses reported many large shooting stars. This time of year is a peak period for various meteor showers. Due to a lack of precise observational data from the witness, GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" because of the lack of accurate information regarding the object's position in the sky, direction of movement, or photographs. The observation is likely a combination of phenomena with different origins.

summary: Observation of the slow movement of a luminous sphere flying over the landscape: a mistake for the full moon at its setting.
description: On the morning of July 23, 2013, the witness observed a luminous sphere moving slowly and silently above the ridge of a mountain near his home. Astronomical analysis and several email exchanges providing additional information led to the conclusion that it was a case of mistaken identity, specifically the moon. The following day, about an hour later, the witness observed almost the same sighting. This type of misinterpretation is quite common when the sky is slightly cloudy. A light close to the horizon is frequently interpreted as an object flying over the landscape, rather than being recognized as a celestial body. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": observation of the full moon at sunset.

summary: Brief observation of the rapid and silent movement of an object shaped like a boater: lack of information.
description: On Monday, July 22, 2013, at approximately 6:15 PM, a witness observed a bright object moving silently across the sky at very high speed. The witness described a silvery, bulbous object, similar to a boater hat. Its approximate trajectory was SE-NW in an area of aircraft traffic at Montpellier-Fréjorgues Airport. This very brief observation (2 to 3 seconds) of a bright object in the sky, by a single witness, is poorly documented (no diagram). The strangeness of this observation lies in the object's speed. Considering that the object covered a 60° field of view in 3 seconds, and that it was 200 meters away, this already corresponds to a speed of approximately 270 km/h. It could be a small object carried by the wind 15 or 20 meters, but this would then be a significant misjudgment of the object's distance by the witness. The weather report indicates a south to southwest wind of approximately 18 km/h, weakening, which could theoretically fit this latter hypothesis. Further investigation would yield little additional information. GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" due to a lack of precise information and corroborating evidence.

summary: Observation of a fixed dark red light in the cloudy sky: probable astronomical mistake with the Moon.
description: On July 21, 2013, around 4:00 AM, a witness was intrigued by the steady presence of a dark red light in the cloudy sky. The witness's observation direction (Courcelles) corresponded to an azimuth of 230°. The witness reported a round, red object four times larger than the Moon, at an altitude of 25°, and specified that the sky was cloudy, with no celestial bodies visible. It was determined that the Moon was precisely at an azimuth of 231°, at an altitude of 4.6°. It is highly probable that the witness was a victim of the classic lunar illusion, which makes the Moon appear very large at moonrise or moonset. The Moon, partially obscured by cloud cover, did not reveal the surface details that would have allowed the witness to identify it. After waking up in the middle of the night, it is common for rare phenomena to greatly surprise witnesses. GEIPAN classifies this case "B": probable observation of the Moon (the notable difference in the height of the phenomenon in the sky justifies this case not being classified "A").

summary: Observation of the silent movement of two colored lights in the sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On July 20, 2013, at approximately 11:30-11:45 PM, two witnesses observed two intense lights in the sky. The first light was orange, and the second was reddish-purple. No sound accompanied their movement and disappearance in different directions. Only one witness account was recorded. This observation of luminous orbs strongly resembles Thai lanterns, but with some unique features: firstly, the reddish-purple color, which is quite rare, and especially the different paths of the two lights. The Météociel weather report for Nevers indicated unstable winds at that time, which could potentially explain why the two objects did not follow the same trajectory. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the silent, straight and low-altitude passage of a craft with 5 colored lights (red orange white) below: lack of information.
description: On July 20, 2013, at midnight, a witness and his wife noticed that the streetlamp was out. They then observed the silent passage of an object with five red, orange, and white lights underneath, rotating clockwise. Its southwest-northeast trajectory was at low altitude, with a steady, slow speed. The streetlamp came back on as the object moved away. The observation lasted 10 minutes. Only one witness statement was recorded. The combination of lights described by the witness and the object's movement suggested an aircraft on approach to land, which is often quiet. Aircraft have multiple flashing lights (red anti-collision lights, flashing white strobes, and steady white, green, and red lights). However, there is no major airfield nearby. GEIPAN did not process this report quickly enough to obtain radar tracks of aircraft flying over this area: this hypothesis cannot be verified. The north to northeast wind recorded on Météociel is contrary to the observed movement: it cannot be an object carried by the wind. The correlation between the streetlights going out and the phenomenon is intriguing, but not proven. Lacking very precise information, apart from the report, GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" due to insufficient data.

summary: Observation of the silent passage of groups of dark red luminous balls: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On Saturday, July 20, 2013, at 1:30 a.m., a witness was intrigued by the silent passage of groups of dark red orbs across the sky. The witness took photographs. This sighting of reddish-orange orbs moving in a line on weekend nights strongly resembles Thai lanterns. It is difficult to correlate their movement, estimated from East to West, with the local wind, which was very weak and variable, and therefore uncertain (northern wind in Colmar, southerly in Belém (see weather forecast). This could explain the change in direction. The witness, who was unaware of the existence of this type of object, researched it and recognized that they could be lanterns. Despite the uncertainty regarding the local wind, GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of a fireball followed by a trail on a downward oblique trajectory: probable observation of a bolide.
description: On July 17, 2013 at approximately 11:45 PM, a witness observed the passage of a fireball followed by a trail on a downward oblique trajectory. The description of a "fireball" lasting 2 to 3 seconds perfectly matches a bolide (atmospheric re-entry of a meteoroid). The witness saw it to the east, moving from north to south. There was no recording by automatic cameras, but another similar report was received by GEIPAN at a very similar time: in Plaisir (78), observed to the southwest, moving towards the horizon (from 60° to 45° elevation). The observed undulation may be a physiological illusion of vision called the autokinetic illusion (see: kinetic illusion). It should be noted that these bolide phenomena, often perceived as very close by witnesses, actually occur at altitudes of 100 to 50 km, and are therefore visible from the ground over an area of approximately 200 km in diameter. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of a bolide.

summary: Observation of the rapid passage across the sky of a white incandescent object without a trail: probable observation of a bolide.
description: On July 17, 2013, at 11:58 PM, a witness observed a fireball (bolide) from their window, following a downward trajectory. The description of an "incandescent object of white light without a trail, very fast" perfectly matches that of a fireball (atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid). No automatic cameras recorded the event, but another similar report was received by GEIPAN (the French National Center for Experimentation on Astronomical Phenomena) at a very similar time: in Saint-Germain-sur-Ille (35), at 11:45 PM, observed in the east, moving from north to south. It should be noted that these fireball phenomena, often perceived as very close by witnesses, occur at altitudes of 50 to 100 km and are therefore visible over an area approximately 200 km in diameter. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable fireball sighting.

summary: Observation of a stationary golden-white luminous phenomenon in the sky: lack of information.
description: On July 17, 2013, at approximately 11:50 PM, a witness observed a bright, stationary white phenomenon from their home. The observation lasted one minute before the phenomenon disappeared, then reappeared for 30 seconds before vanishing completely. No other reports were collected. GEIPAN considered several hypotheses for this case: - astronomical hypothesis: a planet, temporarily obscured by clouds, could have given this impression, but the star chart did not reveal any bright celestial bodies in the Southeast. - hypothesis of a reflection of the Sun on a satellite: the effect would have been roughly the same, but shorter, and not stationary for a full minute. A check with the Calsky website shows several satellites passing through the witness's field of view at the indicated time, as well as two Iridium satellite flares at 11:45 PM and 11:54 PM, but in a direction opposite to that indicated by the witness. - Aeronautical hypothesis: an aircraft viewed head-on, with its landing lights on, can certainly give the impression of a fixed point: it seems to disappear if it changes course, even when the witness is no longer in the line of sight of the spotlight. This hypothesis could not be confirmed in time with air traffic control. This somewhat unusual observation, of moderate consistency due to the single witness statement and the absence of a photograph, is classified as "C" due to a lack of corroborating information.

summary: Observation of the rapid and silent passage of three whitish "dots" in the hazy sky: lack of information.
description: On July 16, 2013, at 10:45 PM, a witness lying on his terrace was stargazing. He was intrigued by the silent and rapid passage of three whitish, triangular "patches" in the hazy sky. A slight halo was visible. The objects disappeared over the horizon after 30 seconds. Only one witness account was recorded. The sky was overcast over Agen. Air traffic was quite heavy at high altitude (7,000 to 12,000 meters) but could not explain the observed phenomenon. GEIPAN considered several hypotheses for this observation: - A nightclub laser: the observation time seems short, and the witness who considered this hypothesis refutes it. - Birds (gulls) illuminated by city lights but immersed in low clouds: it seems surprising that birds would remain illuminated while climbing to altitude. The apparent size (2/3 of the Moon) and circular shape are not well suited to this hypothesis. The witness who considered this hypothesis refutes it. That said, the dynamics of the phenomenon are quite consistent with those of birds. The witness mentions that gulls seemed to react to the phenomenon. - A visual (ophthalmic) problem of the witness or an ocular migraine could have caused phosphenes. The blurred outlines and the impression of flat lights are consistent with this hypothesis. It seems difficult to verify this hypothesis retrospectively through a medical examination. As neither of these hypotheses can be confirmed, and as it is a rather distant and unclear phenomenon, GEIPAN classifies this case in category "C" due to a lack of information or corroboration.

summary: Observation of the movement of five orange light sources followed by a slightly opalescent and transparent ovoid phenomenon: probable observation of Thae lanterns followed by the reflection on a satellite.
description: On July 14, 2013, at approximately 11:45 PM, a witness observed five orange light sources moving across the sky over Toulouse. The witness then made a second observation of a slightly opalescent and transparent ovoid object against the dark background of the sky. The initial observation (orange light sources moving in a straight line) closely resembles the sighting of Thai lanterns, drifting from west to east with the light westerly wind (see Meteociel report). July 14th is certainly a date conducive to this type of phenomenon. The second phenomenon suggests a reflection of the sun on a satellite. The Calsky website did indeed indicate a reflection of this type on the Iridium 70 satellite at that very moment, but observable in the northeast, quite low on the horizon, which does not correspond well to the witness's account. It could also be a reflection on another, unlisted satellite. The coincidence between these two independent events is obviously surprising, but not impossible. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of Thae lanterns, then of a reflection on a satellite.

summary: Observation of the silent and successive passage of luminous orange balls in the sky: probable observation of the passage of Thai lanterns.
description: On July 13, 2013, between 11:30 and 11:40 PM, a witness was intrigued by the successive and silent passage of several luminous orange orbs across the sky. The witness's account and the photographs all bear the hallmarks of a sighting of Thae lanterns: orange orbs moving with the wind (a northeast wind was recorded at Cap Ferret). The time and day of the year are also highly conducive to this type of phenomenon. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable sighting of Thae lanterns.

summary: Observation of the movement of three bright orange points of light: lack of information.
description: witness reported an observation made on July 11, 2013, at 10:30 PM: in the sky, he observed the appearance of three bright orange lights that moved silently from northeast to southwest and then disappeared successively after changing direction to the west. Unfortunately, the lights are barely visible in the videos taken. However, the witness attached a screenshot to his questionnaire. No other reports were collected. This rather unusual observation of a few bright orange lights on similar trajectories inevitably brings to mind the Thai lanterns. However, the observed movement (northeast to southwest, then west) does not exactly correspond to the northerly wind recorded at Dijon (50 km) or Mâcon (60 km), but rather to that recorded at Paray-le-Monial (70 km) (northeast wind). The change of direction could be explained by the effects of local topography, or by a slight inaccuracy or illusion in the witness's perception of the lights' direction. In the absence of very local wind data, GEIPAN classifies this somewhat unusual case as "C".

summary: Observation of the silent passage of several rectangular luminous phenomena with rounded edges: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On Thursday, July 11, 2013, at approximately 11:45 PM, a witness was intrigued by the silent passage of several luminous phenomena on the horizon. The rectangular objects with rounded edges moved from north to south along a straight trajectory. Due to the linear movement of the objects, GEIPAN (the French National Astronomical Society) considered the possibility that they were wind-borne objects, temporarily obscured by trees (see the animation produced by the witness). The Météociel weather report indicated a northeast wind, roughly corresponding to the observed movement (the witness may not have perceived the east-to-west movement, which was a slight approximation from their vantage point). Jaunay-Clan is adjacent to the Futuroscope theme park, which hosts numerous nighttime events in the summer, but the park was not within the witness's field of vision. The evening of July 11th marked the start of the summer evening events in Jaunay-Clan, which may have included some festivities. However, the direction from which the lights originated suggests a lecher on the banks of the Clain River north of Jaunay-Clan. The description of the phenomenon mentions the observation of Thae lanterns, white or red. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of Thae lanterns.

summary: Observation of the movement of a point of light with a very rapid 90° turn: lack of information.
description: On July 7, 2013, a witness participated in a stargazing vigil. At the end of the vigil, at 3:10 AM, the witness observed a white point of light moving in the starry sky above Montchevret. The trajectory of this point intrigued the witness because the unidentified flying object (UFO), directly above their position, made a 90-degree turn in less than 3 seconds, heading towards the hamlet of Romandie. The point was then lost from sight due to the terrain. No trails or noises were observed. No other witness statements were collected. The text of the witness's testimony seems somewhat strange, as it describes a point of light in the sky that suddenly changes trajectory... and it was not an airplane. In reality, it is possible for a satellite's light path to stop when the satellite leaves the area of sunlight, just near the point where the light path of another satellite begins as it enters sunlight. Since these two paths are not continuous, the observer may perceive a single object that has changed trajectory. Further analysis of this type of observation was not possible because the witness was uncooperative in providing information (incomplete or unanswered questions, despite repeated prompts). The observation occurred during a nighttime observation session organized by a UFO group. This context, for some participants, can bias the objectivity of the observation (peer competition, a quest for the unusual), even without the witness's awareness. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as C: lack of reliable information.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of a black and white object in the sky: probable observation of a black bird illuminated by the setting sun.
description: On Friday, July 5th, at 8:45 PM, a witness on his terrace was drawn to the silent movement of a black object across the sky. He initially thought it was a black bird with white wings, but then noticed an "effect" that intrigued him. The observation lasted approximately 15 seconds before the object was hidden by the roof of a house. Only one witness account was recorded. The witness described what he initially thought was a bird with a black body and white wings, but he realized that the white effect was due to a light, like a sweeping motion from top to bottom. This single characteristic led him to abandon the bird hypothesis and conclude that the flying object was strange. At sunset, the sun's rays are grazing on birds' wings and can cause bright reflections, even on black wings. Since the movement reported by the witness is quite similar to that of a bird, the strangeness of this case lies exclusively in these light reflections on black wings, which is not very surprising. See, for example, the images of a cormorant and a common raven. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," a probable observation of a black bird illuminated by the setting sun.

summary: Observations of the silent evolutions of nine orange lights in the sky: observations of a squadron in night flight (Patrouille de France).
description: On July 5, 2013, at 10:20 PM, several people were intrigued by the silent movements of nine orange lights arranged in a diamond shape in the sky. The Patrouille de France's night flights generate a few eyewitness accounts each year. The official confirmation from the Patrouille de France (see the investigative document) allows us to classify this case of a night flight by the PAF (Patrouille de France) as a clearly identified case (category A).

summary: Observation of the silent evolutions of white lights in the sky: observation of the night flight of the Patrouille de France.
description: On July 5, 2013, between 10:40 PM and 11:05 PM, a motorist and his partner were intrigued by the silent movements of several white lights in the sky. Other motorists also stopped to observe the phenomenon. Only one witness account was recorded. The witness's description strongly suggests the Patrouille de France during a nighttime exercise; his account is very similar to other accounts of this annual event (the first Friday in July). Like many witnesses, he was surprised by the silence of the phenomenon, which is entirely explainable by the great distance from which he observed it and because he was facing the aircraft; this misjudgment of distance also made the aircraft's movement appear too slow. The number of lights that can be distinguished depends on the geometry of the formation: some may obscure others. This account clearly illustrates how easily a phenomenon can be misinterpreted simply because the distance to the object is misjudged. This estimation is virtually impossible to make beforehand, even for a trained observer. The searchlights of these Alpha Jets are very powerful, making the aircraft appear closer than they actually are. A very clear sky can also enhance this illusion of proximity. The Patrouille de France confirmed that the maneuvers took place until 11:13 PM that day. This case is classified as "A": observation by the Patrouille de France.

summary: Multiple observations of rapid and silent movements of luminous phenomena in the sky: observations of the night flight of the Patrouille de France.
description: On July 3, 2013, between 10 p.m. and midnight, several people in Apt and Aix-en-Provence were intrigued by the rapid and silent movements of luminous phenomena in the sky. The night flights of the Patrouille de France (French Air Force aerobatic demonstration team) generate a few eyewitness accounts each year. The swift investigation by the gendarmerie and the official confirmation from the Apt Territorial Brigade (BTA APT) allowed this night flight to be classified as Category A, and thus clearly identified. Another observation of this type was made on July 5, 2013, at 10:22 p.m. over Villeneuve in the Alpes-de-Haute-Provence department.

summary: Observation and photographs of the passage of waves of luminous objects in the night sky: probable observation of luminous balloons inflated with helium.
description: On Wednesday, July 3, 2013, around 10:00 PM, a witness, closing his shutters, observed luminous objects moving across the sky in waves for 15 minutes. He took photographs. The observed southwestward movement was consistent with the local wind (see report). The repetitive nature of the trajectories confirms this hypothesis of wind-borne objects. The appearance of the objects did not immediately suggest the widespread Thai lanterns, as the light described and photographed was rather white (like the moon, according to the witness). They could more likely have been luminous (LED) balloons filled with helium, now readily available for purchase. It should be noted that observing at dusk alters color perception compared to typical nighttime observations, and that Wednesdays are less prone to festive gatherings than Saturdays. GEIPAN classifies this atypical observation as "B": probable observation of luminous balloons inflated with helium.

summary: Observation through the side window of a car of a white and grey triangle in the sky: optical reflection phenomenon in a car window.
description: On June 30, 2013, at 10:33 AM, a witness in the rear right seat of a car observed a white and gray triangle in the sky through the side window. He took a photograph with his smartphone a few seconds later as the car passed a row of trees lining the road. Only one witness statement was collected. The strangeness of this case is low. The hypothesis of an optical reflection phenomenon was put forward from the beginning of the investigation and has been shown to be probable (see the investigation report). The witness statement is only moderately consistent, with relatively little usable information provided by the witness, but this may be due both to the brevity of the observation and the young age of the witness. However, a photograph exists that has been analyzed and allows the hypothesis to be supported with relative certainty. This case is to be classified as eAe, as an optical reflection phenomenon in a car window.

summary: Observation of the movement of orange luminous phenomena in the sky: probably Thai lanterns.
description: On June 28, 2013, at 10:58 PM, a witness observed luminous phenomena moving in a straight line above the buildings of Lyon: three orange lights forming a triangle were followed by three more orange lights, also forming a larger triangle. Finally, a single light appeared. No unusual noise was heard during the intermittent observation, which lasted several minutes. The lights disappeared, hidden by the urban landscape. The witness observed and filmed two passes of flying orange lights in formation. This observation was reported in the local press: article in Le Progrès. The witness reported a west-to-east movement, but an analysis of the map and video shows a north-to-south movement, or north-northwest to south-southeast. The objects therefore came from the north, which is consistent with objects carried by the wind (north wind recorded in Bron according to Meteociel). In another article in Le Progrès on July 3, 2013, a lantern release during a private party was reported. According to the weather report, it is not possible that these were the lanterns released in the La Confluence district (south of Lyon) that were seen that evening by this witness. The characteristics of the observed objects—orange balls moving with the wind—point towards the hypothesis of Thai lanterns. The stable triangular formation is common for a lantern release by three people. It is perfectly normal for the three lanterns to remain equidistant if the wind is steady (which is not always the case). These lanterns could have been launched a few minutes earlier, to the northwest of the witness, probably from the Croix-Rousse district, during one of the many private or public parties that take place on the last Fridays of June. GEIPAN did not investigate to find the potential perpetrators of the lantern release. This case is classified as "B": probable observation of Thames lanterns.

summary: Observation of the rapid, straight and silent passage of three green and white luminous phenomena: lack of information.
description: On June 27, 2013 (confirmed by email), at 11:45 PM, a witness observed three luminous phenomena moving silently across the clear sky for 3 to 4 seconds. Two of the phenomena were rectangular and green, and the third was white. White or green points of light crossing the horizon in a straight line in a few seconds could be caused by the atmospheric reentry of meteoroids after fragmentation upon entering the atmosphere. To verify this hypothesis, GEIPAN searched for other eyewitness accounts and video recordings on the Amateur Meteor Observers Database (BOAM), but nothing matched this event. Lacking corroborating evidence to support this hypothesis, GEIPAN classified this case as "C".

summary: Observation of a series of perfectly aligned red and yellow-orange points above a mountain range: lack of information.
description: On June 22, 2013, at 10:30 PM, two witnesses observed a series of perfectly aligned red and orange-yellow points that appeared to pulse or flash in the direction of the summit of Sous-Dine (due south, see map).
