The phenomenon, initially static, quickly disappeared, merging into an orange mass. Only one witness account was recorded, accompanied by photographs. The witness believed they were observing to the southeast, but the Sous-Dine mountain is due south. The witness thought they were observing objects above this mountain; it is highly likely that these objects were much closer, but the alignment above the mountain summit was misleading. Assuming the presence of Thai lanterns, a preliminary analysis of the photos suggests these objects would be located 5 to 10 km from the witness, that is, between La Roche-sur-Foron and the mountain, at an altitude 500 to 1000 meters higher than the witness (who is at 450 meters altitude). Weather reports (Meteociel) from the neighboring cities of Geneva and Annecy indicate a light, very unstable wind this evening: it is impossible to determine the wind direction at low altitude towards La Roche-sur-Foron this evening. The La Roche-sur-Foron Tourist Office informed us that the Fête de la Musique (Music Festival) and the arrival of the Rallye des Bornes took place on June 22nd, but no Thai lantern releases were reported (not even to the Gendarmerie). Due to the lack of possible wind verification with a precise weather report, and the absence of confirmation from local authorities, GEIPAN cannot confirm the hypothesis of white and red Thae lanterns (appearing yellow and red), which is nevertheless entirely consistent with the photos and witness testimony. Pending further information, this case is classified as "C".

summary: Observation of the silent and straight passage of a luminous phenomenon in the sky: probable ISS passage.
description: On June 22, 2013, after 10:30 PM, two people were astonished by the silent, straight passage of a luminous phenomenon across the sky. The description of this rather strange phenomenon (a very bright point slowly crossing the sky) strongly suggests the International Space Station (ISS). The Calsky website indicates an ISS passage from west to south between 10:45 PM and 10:52 PM (see attached Calsky report and the witness's simulation). However, there is an imperfect correspondence between the time indicated by the witness: "10:30 PM, maybe later" and the simulated time. Similarly, the maximum elevation indicated by the witness (90°) is not that indicated by the simulation (17.5°): an inaccuracy in the simulation parameters is possible. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of the ISS passage with a certain degree of uncertainty.

summary: Observation of a fixed object of several changing and flashing colors in the night sky towards the west: astronomical observation of Arcturus.
description: On June 21, 2013, a witness observed and photographed a stationary object of several changing and flashing colors in the night sky to the west. The photographs were taken between 4:23 and 4:30 AM; the witness also kindly sent us two photographs taken during the day from the same location and in the same direction. Given the elements defined in the investigation report (see document), namely the color of the UFO, the very pronounced twinkling effect, and its altitude and azimuth, this case is classified as a confirmed observation of the star Arcturus, located low on the horizon and exhibiting twinkling effects.

summary: Observation of iridescent lights through sunglasses: probable reflection of the sun on the glasses and the camera lens.
description: On June 16, 2013, at approximately 1:30 PM, a witness noticed blue and pink lights in the sky while wearing sunglasses, which he immediately photographed. No other reports of this phenomenon were collected. The witness observed iridescent reflections in the sky in Paris, but only when viewing them through sunglasses; a photograph also revealed the phenomenon. The appearance of the phenomenon is reminiscent of iridescent clouds, but according to an expert from Météo-France, this type of phenomenon only occurs around very high clouds (cirrus), which was not the case here (stratocumulus eleve or altocumulus). GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": an optical phenomenon likely caused by the reflection of sunlight on the sunglasses and the camera lens.

summary: Observation of the successive passage of two luminous phenomena in the sky on a straight trajectory: probable observation of the passage of Thai lanterns.
description: On June 14, 2013, at 11:00 PM, a witness in his yard was intrigued by the successive appearance of two orange luminous phenomena. The description of red dots moving slowly and silently across the sky on a weekend evening evoked the image of Thai lanterns. The Météociel weather report from Blagnac indicated a light northwesterly wind: since the witness saw them appear to the north, they were logically carried eastward. The Calsky satellite observation report indicated the passage of the International Space Station (ISS) shortly before 11:00 PM, on a trajectory very close to that described by the witness, but the timing seemed unlikely. The ISS is generally perceived as a white or yellow dot, rarely orange. Furthermore, there would be no explanation for the second, similar object immediately afterward. One could also consider aircraft taking off from Toulouse-Blagnac (landings are made south of Toulouse with a northwest wind): but the flashing lights would have been noticeable. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of Thales lanterns.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of a very bright bluish ball in the sky: probable observation of the passage of the International Space Station (ISS).
description: On June 13, 2013, at 12:30 a.m., a cyclist observed a bright light which he initially mistook for Saturn or Jupiter. Upon arriving home, the witness was surprised to find that the bluish light passed silently overhead. The trajectory was straight, but the sphere appeared to zigzag at times. It eventually disappeared gradually into the distance. No other eyewitness accounts were collected. Given the objective evidence gathered—namely, that the object moved in a straight line, with slight zigzags, and a brightness and trajectory consistent with the passage of the ISS (International Space Station)—the strangeness of the phenomenon can be considered low, with two possible explanations, one of which is highly probable: an airplane or the ISS (see the investigation report). The witness account is of medium to low consistency: there is an internal contradiction regarding the directions of movement, and no diagram or photograph is provided. In light of these elements, this case is classified as B as a very probable ISS observation, the witness having probably been a victim of autokinetic illusion.

summary: Succession of detonations and observation of a dark oval object whose rear becomes bright with each detonation: lack of information.
description: On June 12, 2013, at 8:40 a.m., a witness and his son, on their terrace, heard a series of explosions and saw a dark oval object in the sky, its rear end becoming bright with each explosion. This object flew straight over the village. The Pan was lost from sight behind a farm building. Only one witness account was collected. The meteorological data gathered showed overcast skies, with a generally low ceiling, a light wind blowing mainly from the south, and average visibility (see the investigation report). This account is of limited reliability: imprecise and lacking in detail, and also missing crucial data necessary for the continuation of the study. There is only one eyewitness account and no photographic or video documentation. The observation could be strange; however, too many inaccuracies and gaps in the account prevent a truly valid assessment of its strangeness. After analyzing the helicopter hypothesis put forward by the gendarmes, and considering the evidence gathered during the remote investigation and the lack of precise information on the size of the unidentified aerial vehicle (UAV), no hypothesis can be definitively confirmed. Unfortunately, GEIPAN (the French UAV investigation unit) did not process this case quickly enough to verify air traffic in a timely manner. This case is classified as category C due to a lack of information; the significant lack of evidence and corroboration prevents a firm conclusion.

summary: Observation of the passage of a luminous orange disc in the sky: probable observation of a Thai lantern.
description: On June 12, 2013, at 10:59 PM, a witness observed the silent movement of a luminous orange disc in the sky. The object disappeared into the clouds. The appearance and movement of the point of light strongly suggest a Thai lantern. The witness indicated that he had seen many others, forming a constellation. It is rare to observe Thai lanterns on weekdays. However, according to someone who rents a reception hall in the area, lantern releases are very frequent at weddings, and weekday lantern release trials are conducted. This single lantern may have been a trial. The southerly wind (according to the Meteociel weather service in Rouen) is not entirely consistent with the northwestward movement observed by the witness, but the particular topography (the Risle River flows along a steep ridge, see map) can cause local winds at low altitudes. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of a Thai lantern.

summary: Observation of light effect movements in the cloudy night sky: very likely observation of light animation of the multibeam projector type.
description: On the night of June 8-9, 2013, around 1:00 AM, a motorist observed silent, bright light effects moving across the cloudy night sky for several minutes. Only one witness account was recorded. The description of the phenomenon clearly suggests a light show (laser?) frequently used by nightclubs for advertising. This phenomenon was also observed in the same location on the night of June 22-23 by another witness. Saturday nights are, of course, particularly conducive to these displays. Cloudy weather (see the Météociel report) is ideal for a very strong effect from this type of projector. The witness's description suggests the effect produced by a multi-beam projector similar to the one in this video: Wedding searchlight hire Nottingham. GEIPAN did not conduct investigations to identify the source of this light show this evening, but the "Le Coyote" nightclub in Saint-Elix-Le-Cheteau frequently uses this type of equipment: it is highly likely that it is the source. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": very probable observation of a light show of the multi-beam projector type.

summary: Observation of the presence then the slow and silent movement of a very bright red-orange object in the sky: probable observation of a Thai lantern.
description: A witness observed a very bright, reddish-orange object appearing and then moving north-south on June 9, 2013, at approximately 12:45 AM. The object disappeared behind a hill. No unusual noise was heard during the 4- to 5-minute observation. This observation of a strong reddish-orange light on the weekend evening, moving slowly across the sky, likely corresponds to a Thai lantern released from Saint-Jean-de-Verges following a festival. Weather reports from Saint-Girons (see weather document) indicate a very light and unstable wind during the night; however, the wind at Crampagna cannot be precisely determined, especially given the low mountainous terrain. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of a Thai lantern.

summary: Observation of the simultaneous and silent movement on an upward trajectory of two polygonal shapes: probable passage of festive balloons.
description: On June 9, 2013, at 8:09 PM, several people observed the simultaneous and silent movement of two objects in the cloudy sky. Polygonal in shape, these two objects, always equidistant, rose into the sky and gradually disappeared into the clouds. The witness's house faces the street, oriented east-southeast, and the living room window, facing the garden, faces west-northwest. The flying object was observed moving from right to left from this window, in the direction of the Senart forest, which is to the left, to the southwest. The object was therefore flying in a north or northeast direction, towards the south or southwest. The witness indicates an east-west direction: if this were the case, the object would have flown over his house. The wind recorded at Orly was blowing from the north at 8:00 PM and from the northeast at 9:00 PM. This wind pattern seems consistent with the observed movement of objects that can be assumed to be helium-filled and carried by the wind. The shapes observed are consistent with the various models of balloons sold at fairs and festivals, which are common on Sundays in June. The relative novelty of the case does not warrant a thorough investigation to find the person who licked these likely festive balloons. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of festive balloons.

summary: Observations two consecutive nights of a fixed white luminous phenomenon: reflection of a street light on an antenna.
description: On June 7, 2013, at 1:00 AM, a witness was intrigued by the presence of a fixed white luminous phenomenon in the sky. He described a white point of light with a horizontal luminous trail and, below it, a curved, pinkish shape. No unusual noise was heard. He made the same observation the following night. GEIPAN (the French National Center for Experimentation on Astronomy, Light and Planetary Diseases) commissioned someone to observe the area around the village at night to look for a possible fixed light, without success. Finally, the witness himself, along with a neighbor, closely observed the phenomenon and determined that it was a reflection of streetlights on an antenna. See the photos: one, rather dark (6730), corresponds roughly to what the witness saw with the naked eye, and the other (6738), a longer exposure, reveals the origin of the phenomenon. This unusual case is therefore classified as "A," meaning it has been fully identified.

summary: Observation of the S-NE movement of a white luminous object: observation of the passage of the ISS.
description: On June 6, 2013, at 10:50 PM, several witnesses observed from their homes the silent, south-northeast movement of a white luminous phenomenon in the sky. The object was then obscured by the landscape. The information provided by the witness, supported by Calsky data, confirms that this was the passage of the International Space Station, visible that evening over the witness's town. The general trajectory (from south to northeast, culminating at 60°) corresponds well to the Calsky data (see document). The brightness perceived by the witness, twice resembling Venus, also corresponds to the calculated magnitude of -4.2 for the ISS under these conditions. The witness described a non-linear movement of the bright point: "like an earthworm." This is a common optical illusion when tracking a very bright point against a black background: the perception of the movement of a bright point in the sky. However, there was a discrepancy of approximately 5 minutes between the time indicated by the witness and the ISS bulletin. GEIPAN sent the witness the ISS pass predictions for June 8th and 9th, and the witness confirmed that this was indeed what he had seen. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": observation of the International Space Station (ISS).

summary: Observation of a beige and black oval object that rotates on itself and remains stationary in the sky: probable observation of a tethered fantasy balloon.
description: On June 6, 2013, at 8:50 a.m., while walking down the street, a witness observed a beige and gray oval object rotating in the sunny sky. No unusual noise was heard during the observation; the object remained stationary. Another person also made the observation. Only one witness statement was recorded. This witness observed a motionless shape rotating in the sky for six minutes. This description strongly suggests a tethered helium balloon, likely a novelty or advertising balloon. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of a tethered novelty balloon.

summary: motorist observed two luminous phenomena in the sky: lack of information.
description: On June 6, 2013, at 10:10 PM, a motorist noticed two lights in the sky that appeared stationary. Continuing on his way, he stopped and then observed two distinct shapes. No unusual noise was heard during the observation and the disappearance of the lights to the north-northwest. The witness took two photographs with a cell phone. No other witness statements were collected. An investigation indicates that the Sun was 8 arcseconds below the horizon (the observation took place approximately 30 minutes after sunset). To the east, the very bright star Vega was visible (azimuth = 65 arcseconds, altitude = 32 arcseconds). According to Meteociel and the weather report from Souillac, the sky was clear, and there was almost no wind. For this observation, GEIPAN considered several hypotheses, such as the possibility of aircraft illuminated by the sun, but 30 minutes after sunset, aircraft at an altitude of 10,000 meters are no longer illuminated by the sun. Another possibility was the observation of stars or planets through a veil of clouds, but no star pairs corresponding to the observation were found. The passage of illuminated balloons or Thai lanterns remains possible, although unlikely during the week, and the witness's detailed description does not closely match typical accounts of Thai lanterns. This somewhat unusual case of distant lights appearing to move slightly remains unexplained due to a lack of information or other reported eyewitness accounts: the case is classified as Class C. The low level of unusualness of the case does not warrant further investigation.

summary: Observation of the passage of a bright yellow-orange phenomenon in the clear sky: observation of the passage of the International Space Station (ISS).
description: On June 5, 2013, at 12:34 AM, a witness observed a very bright yellow-orange phenomenon in the clear sky. He filmed his observation with his cell phone. This observation of a very bright point of light, moving from west to northeast in a few minutes, is explained by the passage of the International Space Station (ISS): the data produced by Calsky (see document) is perfectly consistent with the observation: time and direction. The station appeared in the southwest at 12:32 AM. Culmination was at an altitude of 32° in the north-northwest at 12:37 AM. The station gradually disappeared at 12:42 AM in the north-northeast. The changes in direction described by the witness are explained by the fact that the station's apparent trajectory in the sky is a curve, and the witness, without reference points in the dark sky, readjusted the perceived trajectory into a series of straight lines. The station's brightness gradually decreases from culmination to the horizon; this decrease in brightness is interpreted as a sign of movement by most observers. The witness recorded a video with their mobile phone without stabilizing it during recording, rendering the video unusable. The witness was looking in the correct direction to see the ISS, which was bright enough to be noticed by any observer: if another phenomenon had occurred, they would have simultaneously described both phenomena, which were perfectly visible in the clear sky at that time. This case is classified as "A": observation of the International Space Station.

summary: Observation of the SE movement of a white luminous phenomenon in the sky with a zig-zag trajectory: probable observation of the ISS.
description: On June 3, 2013, a witness observed the southeastward movement of a luminous phenomenon that intrigued him (several different times were given: on June 6, on the questionnaire, he stated 11:18 PM and between 11:15 PM and midnight; and by email, he reported the phenomenon at 10:48 PM (see attached document); on August 2, in the official report, he stated around 11:30 PM). On June 5, this witness observed the same phenomenon at exactly 11:45 PM. The witness observed a very white light, approximately four times larger than a star. The phenomenon moved close to the witness's home. The phenomenon followed a very rapid zigzag trajectory (see the witness's sketch in the attached document) before disappearing from the witness's field of vision. After verification on Calsky, the observation of June 5, 2013, was definitively confirmed as that of the ISS. For the date of June 3rd, the times indicated lack precision to confirm that the witness also saw the ISS (see the attached Calsky document). The changes of direction described by the witness are, of course, inconsistent with the ISS hypothesis; however, this perceptual illusion, known as the autokinetic illusion, is common during ISS sightings. GEIPAN classifies this case as B: probable ISS sighting (the imprecise time of sighting leaves some doubt).

summary: Night observation of lights that were stationary and then moving across the sky: probable observation of a group of helicopters.
description: On June 3, 2013, at approximately 11:30 PM, a witness and his wife observed stationary lights forming a triangle and initially thought they were airplanes. However, as the lights approached, the witness distinguished a dark, flat shape between them. Only one witness statement was recorded. This case was deemed sufficiently unusual by GEIPAN (the French UFO research group) to warrant an investigator to conduct a field investigation. This observation proved to be quite consistent, with two non-independent witnesses and a video of mediocre quality, leaving no doubt as to the reality of the phenomenon, and with a good estimate of its apparent trajectory. The unusual nature of the case was deemed low, as it was consistent with the behavior of various well-known flying objects. Despite some unexplained points (see the investigation report), the observed appearance was consistent with that of a group of helicopters.

summary: Observation of the silent passage of six luminous elements in the night sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On June 2, 2013, at 12:09 AM, four people in the living room of an apartment observed six luminous shapes silently passing across the sky from north to south-southeast. The observation lasted at least one minute. Only one witness account was recorded. The sighting of luminous shapes crossing the sky in just a few minutes on a weekend night strongly suggests the presence of Thai lanterns, likely licked nearby after a private party. The movement is observed from North to South-Southwest, which is consistent with the North wind recorded in Lille (Météociel). GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," a probable observation of Thames lanterns. The witness, informed of this hypothesis, did not accept it.

summary: Observation of the silent and straight passage of an orange ball in the sky: observation of a Thai lantern.
description: On Sunday, June 2, 2013, at 10:59 PM, a witness was intrigued by the silent passage of an orange ball across the sky. He took a photograph. The description of an orange ball moving in a straight line late at night on a weekend suggests a Thai lantern. The witness's photos are perfectly consistent with this hypothesis. Météociel indicated a light northerly wind. The witness reported the object moving from the northeast to the southwest: this change in direction could be explained by local geographical conditions. The witness, contacted by telephone, had seen Thai lanterns since his observation on July 14 and recognized the same type of object. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": observation of the passage of a Thai lantern.

summary: Observation of the movement of a dozen luminous yellow-orange balls: probable observation of the passage of Thai lanterns.
description: On June 1, 2013, at 12:02 AM, several people observed the silent passage of about a dozen luminous yellow-orange orbs that appeared successively in the sky. The witness's description (very bright yellow-orange orbs moving slowly across the sky) perfectly matched that of Thai lanterns. Having seen videos and photos of Thai lanterns, the witness recognized the phenomenon, which he had never seen before. These lanterns could have been released during a wedding that took place 600 meters away. The Météociel local wind report indicated a light west to northwest wind, which is inconsistent with the observed movement (more towards the east). However, a northeast wind was recorded in Boulogne; coastal winds are often complex and vary in direction depending on altitude. Considering all these factors, GEIPAN classified this case as "B": probable observation of Thai lanterns. The low strangeness of the case does not require a field investigation.

summary: Observation of the presence and then the movement of a dark, pebble-shaped phenomenon with two red lights at the front and rear and the presence of a high-pitched buzzing sound.
description: On May 29, 2013 (not May 30 as indicated by the witness in their questionnaire), at 11:45 PM, a motorist observed a black, pebble-shaped object with two red lights at the front and rear, several dozen meters above the ground. The object moved northwest and disappeared behind a hedge. A high-pitched buzzing sound was heard during the minute of the observation. This observation is of moderate strangeness because it does not correspond to typical misinterpretations. The pebble shape reported by the witness is unusual in UFO sightings. The movement of the object was, however, quite slow and linear. There is no reason to doubt the witness's sincerity, but it should be noted that they are the only one to have reported seeing the phenomenon, and there are no photos or videos: this makes the case somewhat unreliable, especially since the witness's description is brief. Further witness accounts could help to better characterize the case, either by explaining it or by giving it more substance. This strange, moderately consistent observation is classified as D1, an unexplained phenomenon.

summary: Observation of the slow movement of a blinking light in the sky: probable observation of the passage of a Thai lantern with an imperfect combustion of the burner.
description: On Saturday, May 25, 2013, at 11:05 PM, a witness observed a slowly moving, flashing colored light with a red halo in the sky. No unusual noises were heard during the two-minute observation. The light rose into the sky and disappeared into a cloud. The witness described a flashing light, white, red, and yellow, moving slowly from the west, rising into the sky until it vanished. The video shows a yellow light surrounded by red. The wind was blowing in front of the witness (see the weather report). The observation is entirely consistent with that of a Thae Lechee lantern in the witness's line of sight, one or two kilometers away. The day and time of the observation (Saturday evening) are typical for the lecheeing of this type of lantern during private celebrations. The flickering light likely corresponds to incomplete combustion of the flame. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of a Thae lantern.

summary: Observations of the presence of lights for 3 consecutive nights, stationary then moving downwards; no noise; disappearance of the UFO hidden by the urban landscape: lack of information.
description: Testimony received in May 2015 regarding an observation made on May 25, 2013. On the evenings of May 25, 26, and 27, 2013 (time uncertain between 9:00 PM and 10:00 PM), the witness (T1) and two other people (T2 and T3) from his family observed the presence of three colored lights (yellow-orange) at low altitude in a westward direction. The phenomenon, initially stationary, then moving downwards, disappeared, hidden by the urban landscape. No unusual noises were heard. The observation was made with the naked eye and binoculars, leading to different descriptions of the UFO (shape, colors, etc.). Only one questionnaire was collected. According to the investigation report (attached), the unusual features were: - stars with an abnormal appearance: for T1 and T3; - the strip of light (seen with binoculars): for T1 and T3. - The movement of lights: precisely described by T1, except for the time, which is certain to be more than an hour past. This is not part of T3's observation. It is confusing for T2; beyond the inconsistencies and contradictions, these movements are not reported spontaneously and therefore do not seem to represent a strong perceived strangeness. T2's testimony does not confirm T1's account regarding these UFO movements. Only two hypotheses are considered for this succession of three fixed and then moving lights over three consecutive evenings: helicopters or drones. But neither can be reasonably considered (probability < 30%). The consistency of the testimony is weak: - T1 has been interested in UFOs since adolescence, was satisfied from the very first night to witness sightings and be able to link them to UFOs, thought about it again in the following days, but didn't think to take photos or videos, nor to call neighbors or friends, not even on the third night, even though the sighting had already occurred two nights in a row. - T1, although pre-sensitized to the strange, waited two years to report his own strange sighting. We don't find in him the fear or restraint created by terror or strangeness that could explain the delay in reporting, since he speaks about it publicly on forums and in the press. This would tend to diminish the reality of the strangeness perceived at the time of the sighting. - Inconsistencies (within the testimonies) or contradictions (between the testimonies) on notable points. The observation has no plausible explanation. However, the evidence is too weak to validate the strange and unexplained nature of the observation. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as C: lack of reliable information.

summary: Observation of the movement of a white object at the center of a translucent concentric halo above the sea in the distance: lack of information.
description: On Monday, May 20, 2013, at approximately 4:05 PM, a person lying on the beach in Menton was intrigued by a phenomenon observed offshore. The witness saw a white object in the center of a translucent concentric halo in the clear sky. The phenomenon moved much faster than an airplane from west to east-southeast, and the witness heard no noise. The observation lasted 10 to 15 seconds before the phenomenon disappeared into the distance. Only one witness account was recorded. The witness observed from the beach in Menton (see map) an elongated white object, surrounded by a perfectly round halo, flying over the sea at a distance he could not estimate. The witness reported a clear sky, but the local weather report (see Météociel) indicated partly cloudy skies (overcast?). This description evokes an aircraft observed amidst a luminous halo caused by the reflection of the sun on the fuselage, according to an atmospheric optical phenomenon known as the Brocken spectrum (see Atmospheric Optical Phenomena). However, with the available information, it is difficult to confirm this hypothesis. Furthermore, the witness believes the speed of the phenomenon is inconsistent with that of an aircraft. Without a photograph or corroboration with other testimonies or measurements, GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" due to a lack of information.

summary: Observation of the silent passage of 6 to 8 orange luminous balls: probable observation of the passage of Thai lanterns.
description: On May 19, 2013, at approximately 12:30 a.m., several people observed from a first-floor balcony the silent passage of six to eight luminous yellow-orange orbs from the horizon to the south. The witness, facing north, observed luminous objects to the northwest and saw them moving southward. The Meteociel weather report for Rouen indicated: cloudy skies, northeast wind, following rain with a northerly wind. This account is entirely consistent with the observation of Thai lanterns: appearance, duration, movement with the wind, time, and day of the week are all consistent with the end of a festival. The slightly rainy weather is indeed not very favorable for sky lanterns, but they still functioned despite a few drops of rain. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the slow movement of a luminous disk: probably observed from above a Thai lantern.
description: On May 18, 2013, around 10 PM, a witness observed, from the first floor of their home, the slow movement of a luminous disc which suddenly moved away and disappeared. This observation, taken from above, of a luminous disc, about the size of half a globe lamppost, suggests a rather small object carried by the wind. The Meteociel weather report indicates a southerly wind; the witness, observing from their first-floor apartment, points to a northerly direction: this could be due to turbulence in the street sheltered from the wind. This long Pentecost weekend was conducive to numerous celebrations, which may have involved the licking of Thai lanterns. The disc shape described by the witness corresponds to the shape of a cylinder seen from above. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of a Thai lantern from above.

summary: Observation of the passage of orange luminous points in the sky: probable observation of the passage of Thai lanterns.
description: On May 11, 2013, at approximately 10:30 PM, a witness observed five slowly moving yellow-orange lights appearing northeast of the city. The intensity of these lights gradually decreased, and they disappeared. This observation, occurring on a Saturday evening, is entirely consistent with the sighting of Thai lanterns released during a festival, moving with the wind, which was very light and variable at that time (see the Météociel report from Saint-Étienne). GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable sighting of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of about forty red balls in the sky: observation of the passage of Thai lanterns launched during a private party.
description: On Saturday, May 11, 2013, at 11:45 PM, a motorist and his son observed about forty red orbs moving silently in the sky. The witness's account suggested they were Thai lanterns, at a time and date typical for such objects. The estimated distance and size of the objects was, as is often the case, very inaccurate. Following the publication of the event in the newspaper, a person reported to the police that they had licked Thai lanterns in the sky over Domancy that evening, during their wedding celebration. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A," meaning it is a clearly identified case: observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of several luminous orange balls following one another in the sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On May 11, 2013, around midnight, a motorist observed several luminous orange orbs moving silently across the sky. The witness reported a low-altitude passage, below the clouds, following a straight trajectory towards Marcais, northeast of Le Châtelet. The witness took photographs, but the originals were not provided. No other reports were collected. According to Meteociel, the wind recorded in Châteauroux was blowing from the west-southwest in a steady pattern (a similar pattern was observed in Bourges). The hypothesis, proposed by the gendarmerie, that these phenomena were Thai lanterns is entirely consistent with the observation and the local wind conditions. The evenings of the long weekends in May are very conducive to all kinds of celebrations, providing opportunities to launch this type of sky lantern. This case is classified as Class B: probable observation of the passage of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation by three people of the movement of two orange lights on the same trajectory at eight-minute intervals: probable Thai lanterns.
description: On May 10, 2013, in Nemours, three people observed a dark, fluorescent orange light surrounded by red moving from their terrace at 10:30 PM. One of the witnesses photographed and filmed the phenomenon with a cell phone for forty seconds as the object moved away. Seven to eight minutes later, the witnesses saw a second light coming from the same direction, which disappeared in the exact same spot as the first. The witness also filmed this second sighting for about a minute. The only witness statement provides a detailed account of this sighting of "a dark, fluorescent orange light surrounded by red, without any trail," and clearly suggests the presence of Thae lanterns (flying lanterns), probably released during a festival. The witness's videos confirm this hypothesis (see YouTube links in the witness's questionnaire). The observed movement from southwest to northeast is consistent with the southwest to south wind recorded over Melun (see weather report). The lanterns are between 50 cm and 1 m in size and fly between 50 and 300 m altitude. This case is class B: probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the movement of orange luminous points in the Parisian sky: probable observation of the passage of Thai lanterns.
description: On the evening of May 7, 2013, witnesses observed numerous luminous points in the sky, flying in pairs. The objects were red/orange in color, without trails. The observation reported six to eight luminous points moving on either side of the Montparnasse Tower in an approximate southwest to northeast direction (see map). The weather forecast for Paris Montsouris (located very close to the witnesses) indicated, according to Meteociel, a light southwest wind at 7 p.m. and 10 p.m., but northeast and southeast winds at 8 p.m. and 9 p.m. The weather forecast for Orly Airport was more stable, with the southwest wind remaining constant during this period. The witnesses did not specify a precise time of observation, only "apero-Dener" (a play on words combining "apéro" and "Dener," meaning pre-dinner drinks). Assuming a southwest wind, the luminous objects would have moved with the wind; their appearance and movement are entirely consistent with Thai lanterns. The licking of Thai lanterns is common on festive evenings, even in cities, although strongly discouraged in urban environments. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," a probable sighting of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observations of a group of luminous objects moving slowly across the sky: probable observation of a group of Mylar balloons.
description: On May 3, 2013, at approximately 4:45 PM, a witness on the school grounds was intrigued by sources of light arranged in a triangle in the sky. They were moving slowly eastward. The witness (T1) alerted another person who also observed these objects. These two individuals observed the phenomenon for a considerable time (30 to 40 minutes) while returning to their respective homes. No other witness statements were collected. Given the elements defined in the investigation report (see attached document), namely the shape, appearance, and brightness comparable to those of a cluster of Mylar balloons floating in the wind at high altitude, as well as the slow movement in a calm atmosphere, this case is classified as B, a probable observation of a group of Mylar balloons. This testimony is consistent, precise, and well-detailed. Two eyewitnesses were present and gave statements, but no photographs (although one was taken) or videos were recorded. The observation is not unusual, as the objects are ultimately quite ordinary, but can take on an unusual appearance under certain conditions. This case is classified as Class B: probable observation of a group of Mylar balloons.

summary: Observation of the movements of a white glow in a cloudy night sky: observation of a light animation.
description: On April 28, 2013, at midnight, a driver observed the repetitive and sinuous movements of a white glow in the low-altitude sky. Her passenger also observed the phenomenon. Only one questionnaire was collected. The observation took place in three stages: 1-a) Around midnight, during the night from Saturday to Sunday, a luminous phenomenon was seen by the passenger in a vehicle traveling on the highway. 1-b) This led the driver to stop the vehicle at the next rest area, 500 to 800 meters after the first observation. The observation while stopped continued for one hour, with both witnesses remaining in the vehicle. The phenomenon was seen above the trees, with an elevation estimated by the witness at 30°. 1-c) As the phenomenon did not disappear, the witness resumed driving. The weather situation recorded in Béziers (approximately 50 km to the Northeast) on April 27, 2013 at 11:00 PM on Météociel, as well as in the early hours of April 28, also on Météociel, indicates 8/8 cloud cover, no precipitation (last very light, the previous day at 2:00 PM), visibility of 60 km, west wind The wind was moving at about ten km/h, with some gusts. This weather pattern was identical to that of Carcassonne, 60 km to the west, diametrically opposite. The phenomenon was unique, luminous (a whitish glow), without a geometric shape, moving across the sky (at treetop level), always following the same sinuous trajectory ("like a bird in flight"), without noise or trail, and difficult to estimate in size, as the witness had trouble judging the distance. When stopped (in 1-b), the witness mentioned that the trajectory was small, passing alternately behind two trees about twenty meters apart. During the first observation on the highway (in 1-a), the witness stated, "We had the impression it was right next to us." Similarly, when departing (in 1-c), the passenger stated, "It's following us." This last comment, on the contrary, indicates a significant distance from the phenomenon since the heading remains the same while the witness is moving at high speed. The date is significant: it falls on the night of Saturday to Sunday (April 27-28, 2013), on the eve of the May Day long weekend, during the Easter school holidays for the Montpellier academic region, from April 20 to May 5, 2013. The surroundings are also unique: the highway, a few kilometers west of Narbonne, crosses rolling, undeveloped limestone hills, presenting a Mediterranean landscape (garrigue and pine forest), dotted with vineyards (see map). There are also small estates associated with wine appellations, including wine cellars. Some are equipped with guest rooms in the heart of nature, with a swimming pool and tennis court. The witness suggests projecting a beam of light onto the base of the clouds. However, he questions the luminous effect of such a phenomenon (regularity of the trajectory, characteristics of the glow), as well as its origin, stating that "there is only pine forest in this area." All these elements lead us to favor the hypothesis put forward by the witness: the projection of a beam of light onto the base of the clouds. Analysis of the photos provided by the witness allows us to pinpoint the location of the shots from the Narbonne-Jonquières rest area (in 1_b), based on the witness's statement, refined by the sight of the pine trees standing out against the sky. This allows us to estimate an azimuth angle for the shots (document: Azimut_serre.jpg). By extending this field of view (document: (Azimut_moyen.jpg), this allows us to determine the area of origin of these light displays. Within this area lies at least the "Château de Jonquières," 700 meters from the witness. The other hypotheses considered (events at Fontfroide Abbey, lighting of the Château de Saint-Martin) are ruled out, as they are outside this area of observation. To confirm this hypothesis by triangulation, we use the witness's statement regarding the first observation (in 1-a), the vehicle traveling on the highway, from 500 to 800 meters before stopping at the rest area. By extrapolating this distance to the highway upstream of the rest area, we observe that before this point, the highway is uphill, widened to three lanes, in a cut through the hills with slopes on either side. obscuring the horizon. Ascending to 800 meters, the highway is on the plateau, the horizon clear to the front of the witness, visible from the Château de Jonquières, located 1.35 kilometers away. This phenomenon, 45 degrees to the right of the vehicle, cannot go unnoticed! Verification element: from the rest area in 1-b, the phenomenon is seen at an elevation estimated at 30 degrees by the witness. At a distance of 700 meters according to our hypothesis, the height of the phenomenon is: 700 * tan (30 degrees) ~ 400 meters, which corresponds to the altitude of cloud cover. All these elements support our hypothesis of a light show (most likely from the Château de Jonquières or its outbuildings. Unfortunately, to date, the owner cannot be reached by telephone to confirm this). The distance of 1.3 The distance from km (in 1-a) to 700 m (in 1-b) explains several aspects noted by the witness: - the low brightness, - the non-geometric shape, as well as the irregular trajectory, a profile view projected onto the undulating base of the moving clouds, - the perceived impression of proximity and tracking of the witness, due to the minimal change in the UFO's azimuth relative to the witness. This minimal change, despite the vehicle's movement, results from the significant distance of the UFO from the witness. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: luminous animation.

summary: Observation of the movement of a point of light in the sky: passage of the ISS.
description: On April 23, 2013, at 9:42 PM, a witness observed a bright point of light near the Moon that moved vertically at a constant speed until it disappeared approximately 300 meters above the ground. This observation strongly suggests a pass of the International Space Station (ISS). A check with specialized websites (Calsky, Heavens-above) confirmed the station's passage, but 5 minutes earlier. When questioned about this discrepancy, the witness confirmed by email that their clock was 5 minutes fast. This case is therefore classified as "A": observation of the International Space Station (ISS). See the attached Calsky forecast for that evening and the simulation of the station's passage across the sky, from the witness's perspective.

summary: Observation of the movement of about fifteen very bright points in the sky: probable observation of the passage of festive balloons filled with helium.
description: On April 14, 2013, around 8:00 PM, a witness observed about fifteen very bright points of light moving in the sky. They were all moving in the same direction. No unusual noise was heard during the observation, which lasted about twenty seconds. Four minutes before sunset, the witness observed about fifteen disorganized points of light moving towards the east, towards the southeast, and appearing to "flash." This observation could correspond to metallic (Mylar) balloons moving in the wind: the wind at ground level was from the south, but soundings taken in Trappes indicated that the wind was blowing from the northwest at altitude, which is consistent with the observation. This type of balloon, filled with helium, can rise very high and last for several hours. Their origin is very difficult to determine. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of festive balloons filled with helium.

summary: Observation of the rectilinear movement of a black sphere that disappears into the landscape: lack of information.
description: On April 14, 2013, at approximately 1:30 a.m., a motorist glimpsed, for a few seconds, a black sphere moving in a straight line before disappearing behind the trees. No other witnesses have reported seeing it. This sighting of a black sphere cannot be explained by common misinterpretations. However, the relative distance and linear movement of the phenomenon make it a relatively unsurprising sighting. The fact that the witness was the only one to have seen it, for only a few seconds, after a very long day, makes this testimony somewhat unreliable: an illusion, a mistaking it for a nocturnal bird, or a vision problem due to fatigue cannot be ruled out. The relatively low level of strangeness of the case does not warrant a thorough investigation. To date, the police report has not yet been received by GEIPAN. For the time being, GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" due to a lack of information and corroboration.

summary: Observation of the slow and silent passage of luminous points in formation: probable observation of the passage of Thai lanterns.
description: Returning home at 12:43 AM on April 13, 2013, a couple observed three bright orange-white lights passing silently across the clear sky. The witness managed to record two videos. No other accounts were collected. The passage of these lights in formation, moving in a straight line for several minutes on a weekend night, suggests the presence of Thai lanterns. This hypothesis cannot be verified solely by comparing the wind direction, as it was highly variable at the time. However, it can be noted that the wind was light, consistent with the relatively long duration of the observation (3 minutes) and the slow speed of the lights, which allowed the witness to film the phenomenon. The video perfectly captures the typical appearance of this phenomenon: a very bright center and a reddish-orange halo. The weather report for Marignane indicates a weakening west wind at 11 PM on April 12th: weather. On April 13th, between midnight and 2 AM: very unstable light northerly wind at 1 AM: weather. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the silent passage of numerous orange balls in the sky: observation of Thai lanterns.
description: Recent report (October 14, 2015) of a previous sighting. On Sunday, April 7, 2013, at 5:10 a.m., a witness observed several orange orbs from his window, silently moving away from his building towards the sea. The lights appeared incandescent, about the size of a basketball. They were not flashing. He took a video and then saw five more lights following the same trajectory. Eight orange orbs were thus observed. No other reports were collected. The observation of pinkish-orange orbs crossing the sky in a few minutes, on a weekend night, strongly suggests Thai lanterns, probably licked nearby after a private party. The movement was observed from east to west, which is consistent with the easterly wind of 7 to 11 km/h recorded in Le Havre (see the Météociel report for the day of the observation). The witness's video confirms this hypothesis beyond any doubt (especially around the 3-minute mark). GEIPAN classifies this case as "A," an observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the slow and silent passage of an orange ball in the sky: probable observation of the passage of a Thai lantern.
description: On April 1, 2013, at approximately 9:15 PM, two people at their home were intrigued by the slow and silent movement of a luminous orange ball, which then moved away more rapidly and disappeared instantly. The detailed account of this observation—"a yellow-orange ball, without any trail," moving with the northerly wind (see Meteociel report for Vichy)—clearly suggests the movement of a Thai lantern (flying lantern), probably released during a celebration on that holiday (Easter Monday). GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of a Thai lantern.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of a very bright orange object: probably a Thai lantern.
description: On March 31, 2013, in Marseille, at approximately 9:20 PM, three people observed a silent, intensely luminous orange object moving in the sky. The object appeared to be coming from the west, passing over the witnesses' homes, then veering to the right and disappearing to the southeast. Only one of the three witnesses provided a witness statement. It was noted that the direction of movement indicated by this witness (Salon-de-Provence towards Aubagne-Cassis, i.e., northwest and southeast) was the same as the wind direction recorded in Marignane that evening. This observation has the characteristics of a Thai lantern (flying lantern): linear movement lasting a few minutes, silent, following the wind direction, orange in color, on a public holiday. Due to the relative instability of this case, GEIPAN did not investigate the perpetrator. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable sighting of a Thai lantern.

summary: Observation of a black diamond shape rotating on itself above a field: lack of information.
description: On March 31, 2013, at 5:54 PM, a witness, while driving, observed a black, faceted, diamond-shaped object rotating above a field. No wind was perceptible, and the sky was overcast. No other witness statements were collected. A field investigation was conducted with the witness. In conclusion, although the witness demonstrated great sincerity, and the interview and reconstruction were carried out properly, this observation lacks consistency due to a lack of corroboration or additional witness statements. The strangeness of the case is moderate to low, as plausible hypotheses can be put forward, but these could neither be confirmed nor refuted. GEIPAN classifies this case as Category C due to the lack of reliable information.

summary: Observation of the rapid E/W movement of a bright orange point framed by white points: probable observation of an airplane.
description: On March 26, 2013, at 12:10 a.m., a motorist was intrigued by the rapid east-west movement of a bright orange point surrounded by white dots. Due to its limited strangeness and consistency (two witnesses, but only one testimony; unusable photographs), this case appears to be a probable case of mistaken identity with an aircraft. It should be noted that radar reconstruction, requested by GEIPAN (the French National Gendarmerie Intervention Group), identified an aircraft flight whose trajectory and timing are consistent with the observation. Unfortunately, the witness's testimony lacks precision, and the witness's interpretation is too subjective. The issue is not the witness's visual perception, but rather their interpretation of the observation based on their feelings (surprise, fatigue, night driving). This case is classified as Class B, probable case of mistaken identity with an aircraft.

summary: Static amber-yellow light in the night sky then changing shape and rapidly approaching the vehicle: lack of information.
description: 2014 report of a previous sighting. On March 24, 2013, at 3 or 4 a.m., a driver observed a small, stationary, amber-yellow light in the dark sky. He informed his two passengers when the light changed shape and moved rapidly in all directions, approaching the vehicle, which frightened the driver. The sighting lasted 10 to 15 minutes before the light disappeared. Only one report was collected. The description conveys a sense of strangeness. This is the case for all reports sent to GEIPAN, as strangeness (to varying degrees) is the very subject of a report to GEIPAN. It is often contact or encounters with the witness that allow GEIPAN to "resolve" the strangeness, that is, to find an explanation. The unusual aspect here is that the witness did not respond to the request for an appointment, despite a follow-up. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as C: lack of reliable information.

summary: Observation of the passage of three bright points following each other in single file across the night sky: lack of information.
description: On March 19, 2013, at 8:30 PM, a resident of Nice (06) observed three bright lights moving in a line across the sky from his home. The observation lasted approximately 10 seconds before the UFO disappeared from the witness's view, obscured by a tree. Of moderate strangeness and consistency (a single, fairly complete witness account, though lacking coherence regarding the weather), this case lacks sufficient external data for formal identification. The UFO exhibits characteristics common to several hypotheses. While mistaking it for a satellite formation or an aircraft can be ruled out, the observation could nevertheless be explained by the presence of a fragmented meteor or a wind-borne object. However, the short duration of the observation does not allow for the exclusion of either of these hypotheses. It is not the witness's visual perception that is at issue, but rather the witness's interpretation of their observation based on their feelings (surprise, brief observation). This case is classified as Class C due to a lack of information.

summary: Observation of 5 bright orange and white points appearing and disappearing in the sky: observation of several airliners approaching or taking off from Roissy-CDG.
description: witness observed five bright lights above a building opposite his home for over an hour. Having observed the UFO with binoculars, he described it as a burning orange. He called the police and had them witness the phenomenon, observing the appearance and disappearance of the observed spheres. The witness took several photographs. The series of photos posted online by the witness clearly resembles aircraft landing, seen from the front. Let's verify this hypothesis (see the representation in Google Earth: DOMONT (95) 18.03.2013 triangulation.kmz): - by analyzing the photo IMG_0873.jpg and comparing it with Google Earth, we find 86.28° as the direction of the distant light source with the greatest angular height, which leads to an azimuth of 86° + 180° = 266°. - On aeronautical charts, the reference approach for runway 27R is on an azimuth of 266° (AIP France CDG document, page AD2 LFPG IAC 13, page 36 of 1306_AD-2.LFPG Charles de Gaulle.pdf). - Furthermore, in image Img_0873_FNA27R.jpg and in Google Earth, if you draw a line from the landing point on runway 27R to the witness, this line passes precisely through the middle between the two buildings. - Just as in image IMG0873, if you draw a line between the three points of light and intersect it with the horizon, you land precisely in the middle between the two buildings. The identification is therefore complete: the witness saw and photographed aircraft on approach to Roissy. Images IMG_0546, 547, and 549 similarly show a departure from runway 09R/27L; images IMG_0688, 689, and 690 similarly show a departure from 08L/26R, coinciding with a takeoff from 09R/27L (a light aircraft taking off well before reaching the end of the runway). GEIPAN classifies this case as "A," an observation of several airliners approaching or taking off from Roissy-CDG. Additional information on air traffic at PARIS CDG: To ensure optimal airport capacity, the runways at PARIS CDG are operated as follows: - outer runways (08R/26L and 09L/27R) are used preferentially for arrivals. - Inner runways (08L/26R and 09R/27L) are preferred for departures. - Parallel movements on dedicated runways: simultaneous movements on parallel or near-parallel instrument runways, where one runway is used exclusively for approaches and the other exclusively for departures. - Selection of parallel runways: two parallel runways may be selected to perform simultaneous movements: simultaneous landings on both runways; simultaneous takeoffs on both runways; landing on one runway and simultaneous takeoff on the other. GEIPAN classifies this case as A: aircraft observation.

summary: Observation of the silent, zigzag movement of a round, golden object in the sky: probable observation of the passage of a Thai lantern.
description: On March 15, 2013, at 7:38 PM, a witness and his son were intrigued by the silent zigzag movement of a round, golden object in the sky. The witness's description (a slowly moving golden ball) suggested a Thai lantern. The wind direction, from the south (see Meteociel report), was consistent with the start of the observation. It was noted that the witness was located north of Disneyland Park (see map), which could have been the source of the lecher. The zigzag path could be due to turbulence caused by the urban environment. The impression of a rapid upward movement is due to the gradual fading of the lantern: the decrease in brightness was interpreted as a movement away. This case is classified as "B": probable observation of a Thai lantern.

summary: Quick observation of a yellow-orange luminous phenomenon in the sky: observation of an airplane contrail illuminated by the setting sun.
description: On March 14, 2013, at 7:16 PM, a witness was intrigued by the sight of a luminous yellow-orange phenomenon in the sky, which he filmed for a few seconds. After turning away for a moment, the phenomenon had disappeared by the time the witness looked back at the sky. Photographic analysis of the photos and video (viewed online) leaves little doubt as to the origin of the phenomenon. This observation is similar to that made by numerous witnesses in Martinique on February 15 (see case of observation Sainte-Luce (972) 02/15/2013). Aircraft contrails at sunset (or sunrise) are often orange, very bright because they are illuminated by the setting sun, and stand out against the dim twilight sky. Certain weather conditions produce spectacular contrails. The aircraft is approaching from the northwest horizon in the direction of the witness, so the contrail is oriented towards the horizon and appears vertical. The contrail is actually parallel to the Earth, but viewed from below, with a shallow angle of incidence, it appears vertical. The object seems almost stationary since it is moving towards the witness, while being very far away (at least 30 km). Furthermore, there is no fixed landmark in the sky to accurately judge its movement. When the aircraft, which is therefore moving towards the Southeast, enters the Earth's shadow, the contrail will no longer be illuminated and will become less bright than the blue-white of the sky, and will therefore be invisible. The witness should be able to witness the same "spectacle" from time to time, but this requires specific weather conditions: clear skies, of course, but also specific humidity and temperature conditions at the aircraft's altitude. It should be noted that many airliners fly in this direction (London-Barcelona, London-Toulouse), so precisely identifying the aircraft would be of little interest. This case is class "A": observation of an airplane contrail illuminated by the setting sun.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of a bright red luminous phenomenon in the sky: probable observation of the passage of a Thai lantern.
description: On Sunday, March 10, 2013, at 12:30 a.m., a witness was intrigued by the presence of a bright red light above Fort de l'Infernet. The light moved slowly without any unusual noise. The phenomenon disappeared as it moved eastward, where the witness spotted a very bright star. No other reports were collected about this phenomenon. Astronomical verification suggests that it was probably the star Vega, which the witness, looking east, saw rising in the northeast. The Meteociel weather service reported no weather readings that evening. The Bourg St. Maurice service reported very light and unstable winds: similar weather conditions are likely in Briançon. The detailed and precise description of the phenomenon perfectly matches the appearance of a Thai lantern. The bright yellow portion corresponds to the paraffin wax burner. This lantern lasts 3 to 10 minutes, exceptionally 20. The time and day of observation (Saturday night to Sunday morning) are common for this type of sighting. The object's movement does not correspond to the perceived wind: this can easily be explained by the fact that winds at ground level and at low altitude can be different, especially in light winds and in mountain valleys. The object's temporary disappearance is probably due to the lantern passing behind a building or pole, and its final disappearance due to the lantern going out. This case is classified as "B," a probable sighting of a Thae lantern.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of about fifteen white luminous points in the sky: probable observation of luminous balloons or flying lanterns.
description: On March 9, 2013, at approximately 8:20 PM, a witness observed the silent passage of about fifteen white lights across the sky. They disappeared, hidden by the landscape. The behavior of this series of luminous flying objects is entirely consistent with the local wind, from the southwest to west, which was variable (see Meteociel report). Reports from nearby stations, St. Jean de Vedas and Aniane, indicate slightly different directions, but always with light winds. The white color described by the witness suggests light balloons rather than Thai lanterns. Light balloons are helium-filled balloons containing a small lamp powered by a very small battery. GEIPAN did not investigate the perpetrator of this balloon or lantern release; it is assumed that the large residential area located southwest of the observer was the likely origin of the release. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of luminous balloons or flying lanterns.

summary: Observation of the silent passage of several luminous yellow balls in the sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On March 9, 2013, at 11:15 PM, a witness on their terrace was intrigued by the silent passage of several luminous yellow orbs across the sky. This observation report has all the characteristics of a Thai lantern sighting: luminous, yellow objects (more often described as yellow-orange), moving in more or less organized groups, following the local wind (southwest to west: see Infoclimat report), crossing the sky in a few minutes, on a Saturday evening in an urban area. Given the low degree of strangeness of this case, and considering the density of housing in the neighborhood, it was not deemed reasonable to search for the person responsible. Although the witness did not confirm this hypothesis, GEIPAN sees no element in the testimony contradicting this hypothesis, and classifies this case as "B," probable Thai lantern sighting.

summary: Brief observation of a very bright round shape in the sky and a rapid disappearance: lack of information.
description: On March 8, 2013, around 7:00 PM, a motorist was intrigued by an intense light in the sky emanating from a round shape that moved northward and disappeared in a fraction of a second. No other witness accounts were collected. Of moderate strangeness and weak consistency (single witness, short observation duration), this case could be a possible misidentification of a balloon, drifting with the wind, or a car headlight reflection on a power line (see Investigation Report). However, the poor quality of the testimony and some contradictory details (weather, difference between the two sketches of the UFO) prevent formal identification of the UFO. It is not the witness's visual perception that is at issue, but rather the witness's interpretation of the observation based on their feelings (astonishment, short observation duration). This case is classified as Class C, due to a lack of data, although some hypotheses are plausible.

summary: Observation of the oscillations of a luminous color phenomenon: astronomical observation of Sirius with strong scintillation due to particular weather conditions.
description: On March 3, 2013, around 11:00 PM, a motorist spotted a sort of white cross among the stars in the sky. A little further on, he noticed the movements of a colored light phenomenon. His observation lasted an hour and a half. The police, called to the scene, observed and filmed the phenomenon's movements. Witness accounts and the video describe a point of light that was generally stationary, but changed color and oscillated slightly and randomly. The star Sirius (magnitude -1.44) was in the direction of the witness's observation (azimuth 225°, compared to approximately 212° recorded by the police), only 15° above the theoretical horizon. Weather conditions (see the Meteociel report) can promote extreme scintillation: falling atmospheric pressure that persists into the following day indicates strong winds at altitude, which cause intense scintillation. scintillation d'etoile. Low temperatures can cause particular atmospheric optics phenomena if there are ice crystals in the air: halos, crosses. The autokinetic illusion (see autokinetic illusion) may also have played a role. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": observation of the star Sirius with intense scintillation due to specific weather conditions.

summary: Observation of the passage of red-orange luminous points in the sky: probable observation of the passage of Thai lanterns.
description: On February 17, 2013, at approximately 7:50 PM, a witness and his wife observed four red-orange lights aligned above the village of Ham. These lights moved slowly and silently towards the witnesses. Other identical lights appeared during the observation, which lasted about 10 minutes. GEIPAN (the French UFO research group) contacted the witness by telephone to clarify the direction of the phenomenon: it arrived at 1:00 PM, facing the witness as he was entering Ham, heading east. The lights crossed the road almost directly above the witness and were hidden by the sugar factory buildings north of the road. The lights were therefore moving from east-southeast towards west-northwest (the witness provides a different indication in the details of their testimony). As the wind (recorded in Albert) at that time was from the southeast, the movement of the objects is consistent with the wind direction. The reddish-orange color of the orbs, their grouping, and the identical trajectories all point to the presence of Thai lanterns. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observations of a phenomenon in the sky: probable airplane contrails.
description: On February 17, 2013, at 10:04 AM, several people in cars were intrigued by the presence of a phenomenon resembling white trails in the clear sky. Two photographs are attached to the report. The strangeness of this observation lies in two factors: firstly, some of the trails were not straight, and secondly, there were many of them. This can be explained by the particular weather conditions that day: the emerging Autan wind, which is correlated with strong winds at altitude, quickly distorting contrails, and specific temperature and humidity conditions that caused the trails to persist for quite some time. This case is classified as "B": a very probable observation of numerous and distorted contrails due to the Autan wind (a period of low pressure and strong winds at altitude).

summary: Recurring observations of the passage of a bright point in the sky: observations of the passages of a satellite.
description: witness observed the same phenomenon in the night sky at the same time every two weeks: a bright point of light passed over his house and then suddenly disappeared. The Calsky satellite survey of satellites visible from Brest that evening showed that the object "Cosmos 2297 Rocket" (23405 1994-077-B, launched from Baikonur on November 24, 1994) entered the Earth's shadow at 8:04 PM, the precise time of observation (and disappearance) of the observed phenomenon. Every evening at this time and during this season, numerous satellites, of varying brightness, are clearly visible (see Calsky survey). However, weather conditions are not always favorable for observation. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": observation of the third stage of the Zenit-2 launcher carrying the Cosmos 2297 satellite, which is still in orbit.

summary: Observations of the presence of several red lights in the sky: probable observations of Thai lanterns.
description: On Sunday, February 17, 2013, around 7:00 PM, two witnesses observed, from their vehicle, a line of red lights that appeared to be stationary in the sky. The witnesses' description is consistent with the observation of Thai lanterns: several red lights in the sky, apparently at low altitude, on a weekend evening. As the wind was blowing lightly from the east (see Meteociel report), these lanterns could have been released from Curgies, probably after a celebration. Because the wind was light and from the east, the witnesses, who actually saw them moving slightly away, could not clearly perceive their movement. This case is classified as "B": probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the very rapid EO passage of an orange luminous phenomenon: probable atmospheric reentry.
description: On February 16, 2013, at 7:32 PM, a witness observed, through a patio door, the very rapid and silent passage of an orange ball in a straight trajectory. An orange ball crossing approximately 45ths of the sky from east to west in 3 seconds suggests an atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid (meteoroid). The absence of a trail and the spirals described by the witness are not incompatible with this hypothesis, but are a priori rare. The BOAM camera network did not record any event at that time, but there are no cameras covering the southern Alps. GEIPAN received no other observation reports that day. Despite some unusual characteristics, GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of a bolide (atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid).

summary: Observation of the passage of a luminous fire-colored phenomenon in the sky: observation of the condensation trail of an airplane.
description: witness reported an observation made on February 15, 2013, at 6:00 PM (local time in Martinique): for about half an hour, this person observed the slow passage of a fiery-colored luminous phenomenon across the sky. The witness heard no unusual noise but managed to take two photographs of the phenomenon. This observation was shared by numerous witnesses in Martinique, who were paying close attention to the sky following the coincidence between the passage of asteroid 2012DA14 and the fireball that fell in the Ural Mountains that same morning. It was the subject of a report on the ATV channel. Aircraft contrails at sunset (or sunrise) are often orange, very bright, and stand out against the dim twilight sky. Certain weather conditions, particularly near the tropics, produce spectacular contrails see http://contrailscience.com/short-sunlit-contrails-look-like-ufos GEIPAN classifies this case "A": observation of the condensation trail of an aircraft.

summary: Observations of the straight and silent passage of a luminous phenomenon in the sky: atmospheric reentry of a stage of the Soyuz SL-4 R/B launcher.
description: On February 13, 2013, at approximately 9:15 PM, witnesses in Alsace and Lorraine (including six people in the Strasbourg-Entzheim control tower) observed the silent passage of a luminous phenomenon followed by a trail in the sky. The phenomenon moved along a horizontal trajectory. Further witness accounts will be collected later. These accounts describe the passage of a fireball identified as the atmospheric reentry of a stage of the Soyuz SL-4 R/B launcher (catalog number 39083, or 2013-007B), launched on February 11 to place a Progress cargo spacecraft into orbit bound for the International Space Station (see the graph of the projected ground trajectory of the object). It should be noted that that evening, only Alsace and southeastern France had clear skies. This explains why this phenomenon, although very spectacular, went relatively unnoticed in France. This case is classified as "A", meaning it has been clearly identified as an atmospheric re-entry of (large) space debris.

summary: Recurring observations of the movement of an object with yellow lights: probable aircraft sightings
description: The witness regularly observes yellow lights in the southeast, which appear, move slightly, and disappear. The witness's observation direction corresponds to the area where, with west or northwest winds, aircraft coming from the south line up on the runway at Orly Airport (see map). The witness only sees the landing lights of these aircraft, which are highly directional: they are therefore only visible when the aircraft is directly in front of them. The aircraft is too far away (20 km) to distinguish its red-green position lights or even its flashing lights. The witness observed the phenomenon numerous times in January and early February, when the winds were from the west or northwest; they did not see them on the 12th and 13th because, with the wind blowing from the northeast or south, the approach to Orly is then from the west. The witness will be able to identify in real time the aircraft they observe by consulting: air traffic This case is class "B": probable observations of airliners before landing.

summary: Observation of the movement in the sky of a luminous object which, during a change of direction, takes on a cylindrical shape of black color: observation of the Marseille-Bastia flight on approach to landing.
description: On February 7, 2013, at approximately 9:45 PM, a witness and his wife observed the slow movement of an object that intrigued them. The witness's description had all the characteristics of an approaching aircraft: a slow-moving luminous shape, then a black cylindrical shape. The time he mentioned, 9:45 PM, coincides with the arrival of the Air Corsica Marseille-Bastia flight, which departs Marseille at 9:05 PM and is scheduled to land in Bastia at 9:55 PM; this could correspond with what he saw. Bastia Poretta Airport is located 3 or 4 kilometers as the crow flies from the observation point, to the northwest. See the attached approach paths for Bastia Airport: the red line indicates the approach path used with a southwest wind, as was the case that day (see weather report). What is surprising is the witness's astonishment, who reports the phenomenon at half the usual altitude of aircraft. It should be noted that the witness was not at home, and therefore had a different perspective than usual. It is also possible that the pilot used a lower approach altitude than usual that day, for reasons known only to him. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": observation of the Marseille-Bastia flight on approach to landing.

summary: Observations of three parallel dark bands in the sky during an Ariane launch: certain observation of shadows created by the sun hitting dense areas of the Ariane rocket's condensation trail at twilight.
description: On February 7, 2013, at 6:40 PM, during an Ariane launch in French Guiana, a witness and his children observed and filmed three parallel lines clearly visible against the lower horizon. The lines disappeared shortly afterward. Considering the findings of the investigation (see attached report), namely: - The appearance of the UFOs is identical to that of straight shadows. - Other similar examples exist. - The position of the sun. This case is classified as Category A, as a confirmed observation of shadows cast by the sun striking dense areas of the Ariane rocket's contrail at dusk.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of round, luminous, orange objects: probable observation of the passage of Thai lanterns.
description: On Saturday, March 2, 2013, at 7:00 PM, two people were greatly intrigued by the passage of slightly flattened, round, orange luminous objects over their home.
