The objects appeared in two stages, five minutes apart, and the observation lasted a total of ten minutes. These objects moved silently from southeast to northeast before disappearing at altitude. No photographs were taken by the witnesses during their observation. The witness's account—round, flattened, luminous, orange shapes, moving alone and then in groups of three, at low altitude (overcast sky), on a Saturday evening—strongly evokes Thai lanterns. The witness's impression of their large size was due to the objects' short distance. The Meteociel report in Lille indicates a variable wind from the Northeast to the East, not exactly along the path of the objects: the slight elevation (Mont d'Halluin, 30m above the plain) may explain the deviation of the flying objects. These indicators are deemed sufficient to classify this case as "B": probable observation of the passage of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observations of several stationary traces in the cloudy sky: observation of aircraft condensation trails.
description: Witnesses observed several trails in the cloudy sky that eventually disappeared one after the other. A child took photographs with their mobile phone. The questionnaire and then the police report recorded these testimonies. The photograph of this phenomenon (taken at 1/125th of a second, very sharp) clearly resembles contrails. Due to the dry north wind (65% humidity, source: Météociel), these trails were short; because of the observation conditions (sunset at 6:01 PM in Le Mans), they were still in full sunlight, while the blue of the sky was beginning to darken: the contrast was then very strong, and the trails resembled flames. When the Earth's shadow reached these trails, they were no longer illuminated and were therefore no longer visible because they were much less bright than the blue of the sky. This case is classified as "A": observation of contrails.

summary: Sighting of a rectangular flying object with green and red spots: probable sighting of a military transport plane taking off from the Istres base.
description: On January 17, 2013, at 5:30 a.m., a motorist noticed a large rectangular object with green and red lights above the road. The witness slowed down and took a photograph with their cell phone. No other witness statements were collected. Following a thorough and well-documented investigation, it was determined that a military transport aircraft had taken off from Istres heading northwest just before the witness's sighting. It then turned south to cross the witness's path at a relatively low altitude. C-17 aircraft are often equipped with green reflectors on their sides or wings: these are the devices that the witness was able to notice and photograph. GEIPAN classifies the case as category B: probable sighting of a military transport aircraft taking off from the Istres airbase. Some elements of the witness's testimony are not entirely consistent with this hypothesis, which prevents it from being classified as category A.

summary: Observations on two occasions of the slow movement of a dull grey cigar-shaped object in the sky: probable aircraft sightings.
description: witness on a chairlift (Bauge side) noticed, at the zenith, the slow movement across the sky of a cigar-shaped object, matte gray in color, following a straight northwest-southwest trajectory. This same observation was made twice over a period of 30 minutes. No other witness accounts were collected. We have two observations made within half an hour and under strictly identical conditions. The presence of a passenger plane could correspond to the overall observation for two main reasons: 1- The witness stated that they did not see this plane, even though it was perfectly within their field of vision. 2- The description matches in every respect: shape, color, movement. However, the second observation could not be characterized. If we refer to the witness's time data, the Airbus A-320 had logically already passed and could not have been in the same location as the previous one. It could be a second aircraft, possibly military (and therefore not detected by Flightradar24), on the same flight path. After investigation, considering the evidence gathered, site visits, witness statements, and searches for other witnesses via the press, this case is classified as Class B: probable aircraft sightings.

summary: Observation of a luminous phenomenon by a pilot: probable observation of an atmospheric reentry of space debris.
description: On January 7, 2013, at approximately 10:50 PM UTC (11:50 PM local time), the pilot of an Airbus A340 reported seeing what he believed to be a piece of space debris re-entering the atmosphere. The observation occurred at approximately 10:46 PM, around 049°10'54"/000°18'53", which corresponds to the vicinity of the flight over Deauville. This testimony is similar to the case of a simultaneous observation in Ardèche at the Col de l'Escrinet (07) on the same date. Other testimonies of this type appeared in the press in January 2013. Given the accounts of the witnesses, the observed phenomenon is very likely the re-entry into the atmosphere of satellite debris, possibly from the Iridium 33 satellite. This case is classified as B: probable observation of atmospheric re-entry.

summary: Observation of the OE passage of a luminous phenomenon: probable observation of an atmospheric reentry.
description: The witness was at the highest point of the Col de l'Escrinet in the Ardèche region when they observed a bright, fiery-colored phenomenon in the sky with a wide, yellow trail moving horizontally from west to east. This case is similar to the simultaneous observation Aero ARA 102 (001) 07.01.2013 by an airline pilot. Other eyewitness accounts will appear in the press. Based on the witnesses' descriptions, the observed phenomenon is very likely the re-entry into the atmosphere of satellite debris, possibly from the Iridium 33 satellite. This case is classified as B e.

summary: Observation lasting 3 seconds of a flash in the sky followed by a ball from which several pieces break off: probable observation of a meteoroid entering the atmosphere.
description: On January 7, 2013, at 4:13 AM, a motorist observed a flash in the sky for three seconds, followed by a ball from which several fragments separated. No other reports were collected. The witness's description perfectly matches the appearance of a bolide (a meteor entering the atmosphere). January 7th coincided with the end of the Quadrantid meteor shower. At the time of the observation, the sky was heavily overcast across all of France, except in the Southeast; the sky was slightly less cloudy in Germany, in the direction from which the witness observed. The very early hour likely explains the single report. This phenomenon had a greater chance of being observed in Germany than in France. There is no record in the BOAM database, probably due to cloud cover. On the same day, but at 11:45 PM, a large fireball was observed over central France (see the case of SAINT-ETIENNE-DE-BOULOGNE (07) 07.01.2013). GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of a fireball (meteoroid re-entry into the atmosphere).

summary: Observation of the slow movement of orange balls: probable observation of the passage of Thai lanterns.
description: On January 2, 2013, between 9:10 and 9:30 PM, a motorist was intrigued by the presence of several orange orbs in the sky. The witness's description is typical of a Thai lantern sighting: orange orbs moving slowly over a period of a few minutes. The holiday season is a popular time for lantern releases. The wind recorded in Vannes was a light westerly wind. Inland, it was probably weaker and more southerly (see the southerly wind in Rennes), which makes the observed movement of the orbs from south to north (towards Neuillac, see map) consistent with this case. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable sighting of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the silent passage OE of two groups of luminous balls: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On January 1, 2013, between 4:00 and 4:30 PM, a witness observed a first group of lights moving from west to east, followed by another group following the same trajectory. The objects moved silently and disappeared over the horizon. The witness's description (multiple points of light, in two groups), the date of the observation (a holiday), and the wind direction (a light westerly wind) are entirely consistent with the observation of Thai lanterns. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": observation of Thai lanterns.
